question: A nurse is about to give care to a 50-year-old man on the ward who has an infection caused by a multi-drug-resistant germ. The nurse must wear a gown and gloves. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wear the same gloves to touch the man and the rail of the bed
option_2: Put on the gown, enter the room and wash the hands after the care
option_3: Keep the chart inside the room so that the notes are made at once
option_4: Wash the hands and gather all the articles before putting on the gown
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Wash the hands and gather all the articles before putting on the gown

Clinical Rationale: The hands are washed and all the articles are gathered before the gown goes on, so the nurse does NOT leave the room once the barrier is on and the hands stay clean at the entry.

Key Clue: care of a 50-year-old man on the ward with a multi-drug-resistant infection, with a gown and gloves to be worn

Priority Principle: Infection control / Barrier nursing

Why Not Others: (a) The same gloves on the man and on the bed rail carry germs from one to the other; (b) Hands washed only after the care leave the germs of the door and the trolley on the gown; (c) A chart kept inside the room carries the germs out on the paper.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because writing the notes at the bedside looks like the careful act of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: MDRO ke client ke liye pehle haath dhoyo, saaman ikattha karo, phir gown.

PNC Exam Pearl: Everything the nurse needs goes into the room before the barrier goes on.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward has a wound that is discharging pus, a fever, a fast pulse and a falling blood pressure. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the blood cultures as ordered and inform the doctor at once
option_2: Change the dressing of the wound and record the discharge in the chart
option_3: Give a tablet for the fever and check the temperature in an hour
option_4: Raise the head of the bed and give a drink of water
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Take the blood cultures as ordered and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A fever with a fast pulse and a falling blood pressure in a man with a discharging wound points to sepsis, so the blood cultures are taken before any drug and the doctor is told at once.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man on the ward with a discharging wound, a fever, a fast pulse and a falling blood pressure

Priority Principle: Safety / Sepsis

Why Not Others: (b) A dressing change does not treat an infection that has already reached the blood; (c) A tablet for the fever hides the sign while the sepsis goes on; (d) A raised head and a drink of water do not touch the cause of the fall.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the wound looks like the place where the care should begin.

5-Second Recall: Wound + bukhar + BP girna = sepsis; pehle culture lo, doctor ko bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Blood cultures are drawn before the first dose of the antibiotic.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 45-year-old woman on the ward has had an intravenous drip for three days and now has redness and pain along the vein in the forearm. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Slow the drip and watch the vein for one more hour
option_2: Stop the drip, take out the needle and apply a warm pack to the site
option_3: Flush the line with normal saline and continue the drip
option_4: Change the site after the whole bottle is finished
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the drip, take out the needle and apply a warm pack to the site

Clinical Rationale: Redness and pain along the vein mean inflammation of the vein, so the drip is stopped, the needle is taken out and a warm pack is applied to the site.

Key Clue: 45-year-old woman on the ward with an intravenous drip for three days and redness and pain along the vein of the forearm

Priority Principle: Safety / Intravenous line

Why Not Others: (a) A slower drip still runs the irritant into an inflamed vein; (c) A flush pushes fluid into a vein that is already inflamed; (d) A site changed after the bottle lets the inflammation spread.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a slow drip looks like the gentle answer to a sore vein.

5-Second Recall: Nass me dard aur laali = drip band karo, needle nikalo, garam pack lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: An inflamed vein is never used again for the drip.

question: A 55-year-old man who takes a drug for high blood pressure comes to the clinic with a dry cough that has lasted for weeks. Which drug in his list should the nurse suspect FIRST?
option_1: The drug from the group whose names end in -olol
option_2: The tablet that removes water from the body
option_3: The drug from the group whose names end in -pril
option_4: The tablet from the calcium channel group
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The drug from the group whose names end in -pril

Clinical Rationale: A dry cough lasting for weeks in a man taking a drug whose name ends in -pril is a known side effect of that group, so the nurse suspects it FIRST.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man at the clinic on a blood pressure drug with a dry cough lasting many weeks

Priority Principle: Lab / Side effects of drugs

Why Not Others: (a) The -olol group causes a slow pulse and tiredness, not a cough; (b) A water tablet does not cause a dry cough; (d) The calcium channel group causes a swollen ankle and flushing of the face.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a water tablet is the commonest drug on an elderly list.

5-Second Recall: BP ki -pril dawa = sookhi khansi common side effect.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cough of the -pril group stops when the drug is changed.

question: A 26-year-old woman who is three days after a normal birth asks the nurse when she and her baby should return to the clinic. Which answer is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give?
option_1: Return if the mother feels ill or the baby does NOT feed
option_2: Come after three months, when the baby has grown well
option_3: Bring the baby for the check fixed at birth and the mother within six weeks
option_4: Come when the cord of the baby falls off by itself
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Bring the baby for the check fixed at birth and the mother within six weeks

Clinical Rationale: The baby is brought for the FIRST check as told at discharge and the mother returns within six weeks, which is the standard follow-up after a birth.

Key Clue: 26-year-old woman three days after a normal birth asking when she and her baby should return to the clinic

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Follow-up after birth

Why Not Others: (a) Waiting for illness misses the check of the womb and of feeding; (b) Three months is far beyond the time of the check of the mother; (d) The cord may fall in days and is not the mark of the mother's visit.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because the falling cord looks like the natural time for a visit.

5-Second Recall: Delivery ke baad maa 6 hafte me, bachcha batae gaye din clinic aaye.

PNC Exam Pearl: The visit at six weeks checks the womb, the blood and the feeding.

question: A nurse reads the report of the wound of a 40-year-old man on the ward and finds a germ that grows only when air is absent. Which germ is the MOST likely cause of such a deep wound infection?
option_1: A germ of the group that causes a boil of the skin
option_2: A germ of the group that causes lockjaw
option_3: A germ of the group that causes a sore throat
option_4: A germ of the group that causes a cough lasting for weeks
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A germ of the group that causes lockjaw

Clinical Rationale: A germ that grows only when air is absent in a deep wound is the germ of lockjaw, which lives in the depths where no air reaches.

Key Clue: wound report of a 40-year-old man on the ward with a germ that grows only when air is absent

Priority Principle: Lab / Germ of the wound

Why Not Others: (a) The germ of a boil grows in the presence of air; (c) The germ of a sore throat grows in the presence of air; (d) The germ of a cough lasting for weeks grows in air and needs weeks to grow.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the boil germ is the commonest germ of the skin.

5-Second Recall: Hawa ke bina ugne wala kitanu = tetanus, gehre ghav ka khatra.

PNC Exam Pearl: A deep wound with dead tissue is the home of the germ that grows without air.

question: A nurse teaches the family of a 5-year-old child how to prevent an infection of the stomach. Which advice is the MOST important?
option_1: Wash the hands with soap before food and after using the toilet
option_2: Boil the buffalo milk for ten minutes every time
option_3: Give the child fruit that the mother has peeled herself
option_4: Keep the child away from the other children of the street
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wash the hands with soap before food and after using the toilet

Clinical Rationale: Hands washed with soap before food and after using the toilet stop the germs of the stomach better than any single food rule, because the hands carry MOST of the germs to the mouth.

Key Clue: family of a 5-year-old child learning to prevent an infection of the stomach

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Clean hands

Why Not Others: (b) Boiled milk helps but does not remove the germs of the hands; (c) Peeled fruit is one safe food and not the whole protection; (d) A child kept away from the street still eats with the hands of the house.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because boiled milk looks like the sure way of a safe home.

5-Second Recall: Pet ke kitanu se bachne ka sabse bada upay - sabun se haath dhona.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands are the first and the last protection of the gut.

question: A nurse reads the report of the sputum of a 50-year-old man on the ward and sees that the germ was stained to be seen under the light microscope. Which stain is the BEST clue to the germ of the lung that slowly destroys lung tissue?
option_1: The stain that grows the germ on the blood of a sheep
option_2: The stain that shows the germ purple in a cluster like grapes
option_3: The stain that shows the germ pink and shaped like a rod
option_4: The stain that keeps the red colour even after washing with acid
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The stain that keeps the red colour even after washing with acid

Clinical Rationale: The germ of the lung that slowly destroys lung tissue keeps the red stain even after an acid wash, which is the mark of the germ of tuberculosis.

Key Clue: sputum report of a 50-year-old man on the ward with a stain that names a germ of the lung

Priority Principle: Lab / Stain of the sputum

Why Not Others: (a) A germ is grown on the blood of a sheep by a culture, not by a stain; (b) Purple in a cluster is the germ of a boil and of a wound; (c) A pink rod is a germ of the gut and of the water.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the cluster of grapes is the picture every nurse knows.

5-Second Recall: Acid-fast stain laal dikhata hai - TB ka kitanu.

PNC Exam Pearl: Acid-fast means the red colour stays after the acid.

question: A nurse must collect a urine sample from a 30-year-old woman on the ward who has a fever, to find the germ. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the FIRST few drops of urine as they come
option_2: Clean the urinary opening from front to back and collect the middle of the stream
option_3: Ask the woman to pass urine into an open bowl kept for hours
option_4: Take the urine from the pad the woman has worn
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean the urinary opening from front to back and collect the middle of the stream

Clinical Rationale: The area is cleaned from front to back and the middle of the stream is collected, so the sample shows the germ of the bladder and NOT the germs of the skin.

Key Clue: urine sample from a 30-year-old woman on the ward with a fever, to find the germ

Priority Principle: Procedure / Urine sample

Why Not Others: (a) The first drops wash the germs of the urinary opening into the bottle; (c) Urine kept open for hours lets germs grow that were never in the bladder; (d) A pad holds the germs of the skin and of the stool along with the urine.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the FIRST drops look like the fastest way to fill the bottle.

5-Second Recall: Culture ke liye mid-stream urine - pehle saaf karo, beech ka paani lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A clean catch of the middle of the stream is the sample for a culture.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 70-year-old woman on the ward has taken a drug against the germs for five days and now has thin watery stools with a foul smell. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Change the drug against the germs by the nurse's own decision
option_2: Give a tablet to stop the stools and record it in the chart
option_3: Inform the doctor and save a stool sample for the test of the toxin
option_4: Give more fluids by mouth and watch for a day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Inform the doctor and save a stool sample for the test of the toxin

Clinical Rationale: Watery stools during a course of a drug against the germs may be the bowel germ that grows when the normal germs die, so the doctor is told and a stool sample is saved for the test of the toxin.

Key Clue: 70-year-old woman on the ward given a drug against the germs for five days with thin watery stools

Priority Principle: Safety / Bowel infection

Why Not Others: (a) A nurse does not change a drug against the germs by her own decision; (b) A tablet that stops the stools holds the toxin inside the bowel; (d) Fluids help the body but do not find the cause of the stools.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because stopping the stools looks like the kind answer to a bad belly.

5-Second Recall: Antibiotic ke dauran paat = C. difficile, stool test ke liye rokna.

PNC Exam Pearl: The stools of a drug against the germs are tested and never stopped first.

question: A community health nurse is told by a mother that a 4-year-old child in her area has a fever and a rash that the doctor has named as a notified disease. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the neighbours to keep their children at home
option_2: Visit the home and teach the mother about the food of the child
option_3: Give the vaccine of the disease to the child at once
option_4: Report the case to the medical officer of the area within the time the law gives
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Report the case to the medical officer of the area within the time the law gives

Clinical Rationale: A notified disease is reported to the medical officer within the time the law allows, so that the watch on the illness can begin and an outbreak can be stopped.

Key Clue: 4-year-old child in the area of the nurse with a notified disease named by the doctor

Priority Principle: Legal / Notified disease

Why Not Others: (a) Telling the neighbours is a help but is not the legal first step; (b) A visit and teaching come after the report and not before it; (c) A vaccine given after the illness has begun does not treat the child.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the home visit looks like the FIRST duty of a community nurse.

5-Second Recall: Notified disease = turant medical officer ko report karna zaroori hai.

PNC Exam Pearl: The report of a notified disease is a duty of the law and not a choice.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse prepares to collect a blood sample from a 45-year-old man on the ward for a culture. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the vein site with the disinfectant in widening circles and let it dry
option_2: Tie the tourniquet and feel the vein with a gloved finger
option_3: Draw the blood and push the sample into the culture bottle
option_4: Ask the man to clench and open his fist many times
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the vein site with the disinfectant in widening circles and let it dry

Clinical Rationale: The site is cleaned with the disinfectant in widening circles and left to dry, because the germs of the skin must die before the needle goes in or the culture shows them and NOT the germs of the blood.

Key Clue: blood sample from a 45-year-old man on the ward for a culture

Priority Principle: Procedure / Blood culture

Why Not Others: (b) A finger felt over a cleaned site brings the germs of the glove back; (c) A sample pushed in without a clean site grows the germs of the skin; (d) Working the fist helps the vein but does not clean the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the band on the arm looks like the FIRST step of any blood test.

5-Second Recall: Blood culture se pehle site ko saaf karke sukhne do.

PNC Exam Pearl: A wet disinfectant has not finished its work of killing the germs.

question: A nurse notes that a 60-year-old man on the ward with a urinary catheter has cloudy urine with a smell and a fever of new onset. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Take the catheter out and ask the man to pass urine himself
option_2: Wash the catheter with normal saline and empty the bag
option_3: Send a urine sample for a culture and inform the doctor
option_4: Give more water and note the colour of the urine hourly
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Send a urine sample for a culture and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Cloudy urine with a smell and a new fever in a man with a catheter points to an infection of the urinary tract, so a culture is sent and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man on the ward with a urinary catheter, cloudy urine with a smell and a new fever

Priority Principle: Safety / Catheter infection

Why Not Others: (a) A catheter removed before the culture may leave the bladder without a way to drain; (b) A wash of the catheter pushes germs up and hides the finding; (d) Water and a note of the colour delay the drug for the infection.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because washing the catheter looks like cleaning the bladder.

5-Second Recall: Catheter + dhundhla peshaab + bukhar = UTI, culture bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A new fever with a catheter is treated as an infection until a test says no.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse is about to give care to a 35-year-old woman on the ward who has an illness that spreads by droplets from the breath. Which protection is the MOST important for the nurse to set up before entering?
option_1: A cap for the hair of the head
option_2: A gown and a pair of gloves for the skin
option_3: A pair of goggles for the eyes
option_4: A fitted mask that filters the small droplets from the breath
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A fitted mask that filters the small droplets from the breath

Clinical Rationale: An illness that spreads by droplets enters through the air, so a fitted mask that filters the small droplets is the FIRST protection of the nurse.

Key Clue: care of a 35-year-old woman on the ward with an illness that spreads by droplets from the breath

Priority Principle: Infection control / Droplet precautions

Why Not Others: (a) A cap protects the hair and has nothing to do with the breath; (b) A gown and gloves protect the skin and not the breath; (c) Goggles protect the eyes from a splash, not from droplets in the air.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the gown and gloves are the barriers every nurse reaches for FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Droplet bimari = pehle mask, phir baaki barriers.

PNC Exam Pearl: The protection is chosen by the way the illness travels.

question: A nurse collects a sputum sample from a 55-year-old man on the ward for a test of the germs. Which instruction should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Take a deep breath and cough the sputum from deep in the chest into the clean bottle
option_2: Rinse the mouth with mouthwash and spit the saliva into the bottle
option_3: Collect the sample FIRST thing after the lunch of the day
option_4: Collect the sputum into any clean bottle at hand
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Take a deep breath and cough the sputum from deep in the chest into the clean bottle

Clinical Rationale: A deep breath and a cough from deep in the chest bring the sputum of the lung and NOT the saliva of the mouth, and a clean bottle keeps the sample free of germs from outside.

Key Clue: sputum sample from a 55-year-old man on the ward for a test of the germs

Priority Principle: Procedure / Sputum sample

Why Not Others: (b) A mouthwash kills the germs of the mouth and the saliva is not the sputum of the lung; (c) The best samples come in the early morning and not after lunch; (d) Any bottle at hand may carry germs that were never in the lung.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a clean mouth looks like the way to a clean sample.

5-Second Recall: Sputum = chest se gehri khansi se lo, muh ki thook nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The sample of the lung comes from a deep cough and not from the throat.

question: A nurse reads the report of the wound of a 30-year-old man on the ward and sees a germ that is purple in a cluster under the microscope. Which germ is the MOST likely to be shown?
option_1: The germ of the rod group that lives in the gut
option_2: The germ of the cluster group that causes a boil and a wound of pus
option_3: The germ of the chain group that causes a sore throat
option_4: The germ that grows only when air is absent
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The germ of the cluster group that causes a boil and a wound of pus

Clinical Rationale: A germ that is purple in a cluster is the common germ of the skin that causes a boil and a wound of pus.

Key Clue: wound report of a 30-year-old man on the ward with a germ that is purple in a cluster

Priority Principle: Lab / Germ of the wound

Why Not Others: (a) A rod of the gut is pink and not purple; (c) A germ of the chain group causes a sore throat and not a boil; (d) A germ that grows without air is seen deep in a wound and is not purple in a cluster.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the rod of the gut is the commonest germ of the body.

5-Second Recall: Purple clusters = Staphylococcus, boil aur pus ka kitanu.

PNC Exam Pearl: Purple in a cluster is the mark of the germ of the skin.

question: A nurse must collect a sample from the wound of a 50-year-old woman on the ward for a culture. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the skin around the wound and take the fresh discharge from deep in it
option_2: Swab the old dressing that has been on the wound for a day
option_3: Take the swab from the skin at the edge of the wound
option_4: Collect the pus that has dried on the bandage of the morning
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the skin around the wound and take the fresh discharge from deep in it

Clinical Rationale: The skin is cleaned and the fresh discharge is taken from deep in the wound, because the sample must show the germs of the wound and NOT the germs of the skin or of the dressing.

Key Clue: sample from the wound of a 50-year-old woman on the ward for a culture

Priority Principle: Procedure / Wound culture

Why Not Others: (b) A dressing holds the germs of the air and the old blood of a day; (c) The skin at the edge holds the germs of the skin and not of the wound; (d) Dried pus has dead germs and dead cells that mislead the laboratory.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the dressing looks like the easy place to find the pus.

5-Second Recall: Wound culture = gehraai se fresh pus lo, skin pehle saaf karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A culture is only as true as the place the sample came from.

question: A nurse cares for a 3-year-old child on the ward who is on contact precautions for an infection of the gut. Which toy is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give the child?
option_1: A set of blocks shared with the child in the next bed
option_2: A soft toy of cotton wool from the toy box of the ward
option_3: A picture book from the shelf shared by the ward
option_4: A plastic toy that can be washed and kept for this child alone
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A plastic toy that can be washed and kept for this child alone

Clinical Rationale: A plastic toy that is washed and kept for this child alone cannot carry the germs to another child, which is the risk of every shared toy on contact precautions.

Key Clue: 3-year-old child on the ward on contact precautions for an infection of the gut

Priority Principle: Safety / Contact precautions

Why Not Others: (a) Shared blocks carry the germs of two children; (b) A soft toy soaks up the germs and cannot be washed clean; (c) A shared book passes from hand to hand on the ward.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a soft toy looks like the kindest gift for a frightened child.

5-Second Recall: Contact precaution me washable toy, sirf usi bachche ke liye.

PNC Exam Pearl: Everything that goes into the room stays in the room or is disinfected.

question: A nurse reads the blood report of a 65-year-old man on the ward and sees a rise of the white cells with a shift to the young forms. What is the MOST likely meaning of this report?
option_1: The bone marrow of the man has stopped working
option_2: The man has an infection caused by a virus
option_3: The body is fighting an infection caused by bacteria
option_4: The man has lost much blood in the last few days
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The body is fighting an infection caused by bacteria

Clinical Rationale: A rise of the white cells with young forms on the report is the sign of a bacterial infection that the marrow has joined to fight.

Key Clue: blood report of a 65-year-old man on the ward with a rise of the white cells and a shift to young forms

Priority Principle: Lab / Blood report

Why Not Others: (a) A marrow that has stopped shows few white cells and not many; (b) A viral infection often lowers or hardly moves the white cells; (d) A loss of blood shows in the red cells and the iron of the report.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a viral illness is the commonest fever in a home.

5-Second Recall: WBC badhna + young cells = bacterial infection lad raha hai.

PNC Exam Pearl: A left shift is the marrow sending out its young cells.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse must arrange a room for a 45-year-old man on the ward who has an infection that spreads through the air over a long distance. Which room is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to arrange?
option_1: A room of positive pressure, with clean air pushed inside
option_2: A room of negative pressure, with the air flowing out and NOT into the corridor
option_3: Any single room with the door open so that the nurse can watch the man
option_4: A room shared with another man who has the same drug order
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A room of negative pressure, with the air flowing out and NOT into the corridor

Clinical Rationale: An infection that spreads through the air needs a room of negative pressure, so that the air of the room flows out and the germs never reach the corridor where others breathe.

Key Clue: 45-year-old man on the ward with an infection that spreads through the air over a long distance

Priority Principle: Infection control / Airborne precautions

Why Not Others: (a) Positive pressure pushes the germs of the room into the corridor; (c) An open door lets the air of the room mix with the corridor; (d) Sharing a room by drug order and not by germ spreads the wrong illness.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because clean air pushed in looks like the safer room of the two.

5-Second Recall: Airborne bimari = negative pressure room, air bahar jaaye.

PNC Exam Pearl: The air of an airborne room leaves and never enters the corridor.

question: A nurse must collect a throat sample from an 8-year-old child on the ward who has a sore throat and a fever. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the child a drink of water so that the throat is clean
option_2: Ask the child to open the mouth wide and say a long 'ah' under a good light
option_3: Press the tongue down with a bare finger and swab quickly
option_4: Collect the sample while the child is crying loudly
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Ask the child to open the mouth wide and say a long 'ah' under a good light

Clinical Rationale: The mouth is opened wide with a long 'ah' under a good light so that the swab reaches the tonsils and NOT the tongue or the teeth, and the sample shows the germ of the throat.

Key Clue: throat sample from an 8-year-old child on the ward with a sore throat and a fever

Priority Principle: Procedure / Throat swab

Why Not Others: (a) A drink of water washes the germs off the place the swab must touch; (c) A bare finger carries the germs of the nurse into the mouth; (d) A crying child cannot hold the mouth open for the swab.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a rinse before a test looks like the way to a clean sample.

5-Second Recall: Throat swab = muh kholo, 'aa' bolo, tonsil ko swab karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The throat swab touches the tonsils and never the tongue.

question: A nurse on the ward teaches a group of new staff the single MOST important act that stops infection and protects every client. Which act should the nurse name?
option_1: Washing the hands before and after every care of every client
option_2: Wearing gloves for every touch of every client
option_3: Wearing a mask for every round of the ward
option_4: Cleaning the floors of the ward twice in a shift
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Washing the hands before and after every care of every client

Clinical Rationale: The hands carry more germs from client to client than any other thing on the ward, so washing the hands before and after every care is the single MOST important act.

Key Clue: teaching a group of new staff about the single act that stops infection on the ward

Priority Principle: Infection control / Clean hands

Why Not Others: (b) Gloves protect the hands of the nurse and are not clean between clients; (c) A mask worn on every round protects the breath and not the hands; (d) A clean floor cannot stop the germs that travel on the hands.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because gloves look like the stronger barrier of the two.

5-Second Recall: Infection rokne ka sabse bada hathiyar - haath dhona.

PNC Exam Pearl: The hands are washed even when the gloves have been worn.

question: A 50-year-old man on the ward is taking a drug against the germs and asks the nurse whether he should stop the tablets now that the fever has gone after two days. Which answer is the BEST that the nurse can give?
option_1: Save the tablets left for the next time the fever comes
option_2: Stop the tablets at once, because the fever has gone and the drug is no longer needed
option_3: Take half the tablets left, because the body has already won
option_4: Take the full course as ordered, because the germs return stronger if the course is cut short
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Take the full course as ordered, because the germs return stronger if the course is cut short

Clinical Rationale: The full course is taken as ordered, because the germs that survive a short course grow strong against the drug and the illness returns in a form that the drug cannot touch.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man on the ward taking a drug against the germs who wants to stop the tablets after the fever has gone

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Full course of the drug

Why Not Others: (a) Leftover tablets of an old illness are never the drug for a new one; (b) A stop at two days leaves the strongest germs alive in the body; (c) Half a course is the same as a short course and breeds resistance.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a fever that has gone looks like the proof that the body is well.

5-Second Recall: Bukhar gaya to antibiotic band nahi - poora course khatam karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A course cut short teaches the germs to resist the drug.

question: A nurse puts on sterile gloves to change the dressing of a wound on the belly of a 55-year-old woman on the ward, and then touches the rail of the bed with one glove. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wipe the glove with a spirit swab and go on with the dressing
option_2: Change only the glove that touched the rail and go on with the dressing
option_3: Take both gloves off, wash the hands and put on a fresh pair of sterile gloves
option_4: Go on with the dressing and touch the wound with the glove that did NOT touch the rail
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Take both gloves off, wash the hands and put on a fresh pair of sterile gloves

Clinical Rationale: One glove that has touched an unclean rail has spoilt the sterile field, so both gloves come off, the hands are washed and a fresh sterile pair goes on before the wound is touched.

Key Clue: sterile gloves of a nurse during a dressing, with one glove that touched the rail of the bed

Priority Principle: Infection control / Sterile field

Why Not Others: (a) A wipe with the spirit does not make a glove sterile again; (b) One fresh glove over a hand that touched the rail is still not clean; (d) A dressing done with a glove that touched the rail takes the germs to the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a wipe with the spirit looks like the quick save of a busy shift.

5-Second Recall: Sterile glove gaya = dono utaro, haath dhoyo, naya pehno.

PNC Exam Pearl: When in doubt of the sterility, the field is spoilt and begun again.

question: A nurse cares for a 40-year-old man on the ward who has a fear of germs and washes his hands fifty times a day. The man now asks to wash again. Which reply should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: Tell him the hands are clean and forbid the washing at once
option_2: Acknowledge the fear and sit with him, using the plan of therapy agreed with the team
option_3: Allow the washing because clean hands stop infection
option_4: Give him a tablet to calm him and leave the room
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Acknowledge the fear and sit with him, using the plan of therapy agreed with the team

Clinical Rationale: The fear is acknowledged and the nurse sits with the man and follows the plan of therapy agreed with the team, because a sudden stop of the washing raises the fear and a permission feeds it.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man on the ward with a fear of germs who washes his hands fifty times a day and asks to wash again

Priority Principle: Psychosocial / Fear of germs

Why Not Others: (a) A forbidding word fights the fear and makes it stronger; (c) A permission agrees with the illness and not with the man; (d) A tablet without the plan of the team is not the care of the fear.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because clean hands look like the answer that any nurse would give.

5-Second Recall: Handwashing compulsion = dar ko accept karo, therapy plan follow karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The fear is real to the man even when the hands are clean.

question: A 70-year-old woman on the ward has low immunity because of a cancer chemotherapy drug, and she sits in the day room at the hour of the visitors. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask every visitor of the ward to wash the hands at the door
option_2: Give the woman a mask and let her stay among the visitors
option_3: Move the woman to her room and ask the visitor with a cough to wait outside
option_4: Put a sign on the door of the day room that forbids the visitors
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Move the woman to her room and ask the visitor with a cough to wait outside

Clinical Rationale: A woman with low immunity is moved from the crowd and the visitor with a cough is kept outside, because her body cannot fight even the common germs of the air.

Key Clue: 70-year-old woman on the ward with low immunity from a cancer chemotherapy drug, sitting in the day room

Priority Principle: Infection control / Low immunity

Why Not Others: (a) A wash at the door helps the whole ward and not the woman in the crowd; (b) A mask on the woman helps the breath but not the germs of touch; (d) A sign forbids nobody who cannot read it in time.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a mask looks like the whole protection of the breath.

5-Second Recall: Neutropenia = bheed se door, khansi wale visitor andar nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The client with no immunity is protected from the crowd, not the crowd from her.

question: A nurse reads the blood report of a 35-year-old woman on the ward who has had a fever for ten days, and sees a test that names the germ by the reaction of the body's own antibodies. Which test is the MOST likely to have been used?
option_1: A count of the white cells of the blood of the woman
option_2: A stain that shows the germ under the light of the laboratory
option_3: A growth of the germ on the blood of a sheep in a dish
option_4: A test that finds the antibodies of the body against the germ in the serum
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A test that finds the antibodies of the body against the germ in the serum

Clinical Rationale: A germ named by the reaction of the body's antibodies in the serum is found by a serologic test, which reads the antibodies and NOT the germ itself.

Key Clue: blood report of a 35-year-old woman on the ward with a fever for ten days and a germ named by the body's antibodies

Priority Principle: Lab / Serologic test

Why Not Others: (a) A count of the white cells says only that a fight is going on; (b) A stain shows the germ itself and not the antibodies of the body; (c) A growth on a dish is a culture and not a reaction of the serum.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a dish of blood is the picture of a laboratory that every nurse carries.

5-Second Recall: Serology = body ke antibodies se germ pehchanna.

PNC Exam Pearl: The serum tells which germs the body has met.

question: A nurse must shift a 50-year-old man on the ward who has an infected wound of the leg to a single room. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the man and the family the reason for the shift in simple words
option_2: Move the man on the trolley and settle him before saying a word
option_3: Call the housekeeping staff to clean the old bed after the move
option_4: Write the order for the shift in the chart before the man is told
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Tell the man and the family the reason for the shift in simple words

Clinical Rationale: The man and the family are told the reason for the shift FIRST, because a move that feels like a punishment cuts the trust that the care of an infected wound needs.

Key Clue: 50-year-old man on the ward with an infected wound of the leg to be shifted to a single room

Priority Principle: Communication / Isolation teaching

Why Not Others: (b) A move without a word leaves the man feeling shut away like a danger; (c) Cleaning the bed is needed but is not the first step; (d) A written order does not take the place of a spoken word.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the trolley looks like the practical FIRST step of a shift.

5-Second Recall: Isolation shift se pehle client aur family ko samjhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Isolation is explained as protection of others and never as a punishment.

question: A nurse collects a sample of the spinal fluid of a 25-year-old man on the ward who has a stiff neck and a fever. Which action should the nurse take with the sample FIRST?
option_1: Keep it in the fridge of the ward until the morning round
option_2: Send it to the laboratory at once, because the germs die fast outside the body
option_3: Warm it to the heat of the body and send it with the next batch
option_4: Add the drug against the germs to the bottle so that the germs stay alive
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Send it to the laboratory at once, because the germs die fast outside the body

Clinical Rationale: The sample goes to the laboratory at once, because the germs of the spinal fluid are delicate and die fast outside the body, and a dead germ cannot be named.

Key Clue: sample of the spinal fluid of a 25-year-old man on the ward with a stiff neck and a fever

Priority Principle: Procedure / Sample of the spine

Why Not Others: (a) A fridge kills the delicate germs of the spine faster than the room; (c) The heat of the body helps some germs and the delay kills others; (d) A drug in the bottle kills the very germ the laboratory must name.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a fridge looks like the safe place for any sample.

5-Second Recall: CSF sample turant lab bhejo - kitanu jaldi marte hain.

PNC Exam Pearl: Samples of the spinal fluid never wait for a round.

question: A nurse teaches a class of mothers in the village about puerperal fever. Which advice is the MOST important to prevent it in a mother and her baby?
option_1: Wash the hands before every touch of the baby and keep the birth place clean
option_2: Give the mother a hot drink after every feed of the baby
option_3: Keep the mother in bed for the full forty days without a bath
option_4: Put ash on the cord of the baby to dry it fast
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wash the hands before every touch of the baby and keep the birth place clean

Clinical Rationale: Clean hands at every touch and a clean birth place stop the germs that bring puerperal fever, which enters by the hands and by the dirty blades and clothes of the birth.

Key Clue: class of mothers in the village learning about puerperal fever

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Clean birth

Why Not Others: (b) A hot drink comforts the mother and does not stop the germs; (c) Forty days without a bath lets the germs grow on the skin; (d) Ash on the cord invites the germ of lockjaw into the baby.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because ash on the cord looks like the old wisdom of the village.

5-Second Recall: Puerperal fever = saaf haath aur saaf delivery se bachti hai.

PNC Exam Pearl: A clean birth is the cheapest protection of the mother and the baby.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse manager learns that a nurse on the ward has cared for a 40-year-old man with open tuberculosis without a mask for two days. Which action should the manager take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the nurse to be careful in the future and close the matter
option_2: Give the nurse a written warning for the lapse of the mask
option_3: Move the nurse to another ward for a month
option_4: Send the nurse for the tuberculosis test as per the protocol of the hospital
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the nurse for the tuberculosis test as per the protocol of the hospital

Clinical Rationale: The nurse who breathed the air of open tuberculosis is sent for the test as per the protocol, because the health of the staff and the safety of the clients of the whole ward depend on an early finding.

Key Clue: nurse on the ward who cared for a 40-year-old man with open tuberculosis without a mask for two days

Priority Principle: Management / Safety of the staff

Why Not Others: (a) A word of care without a test leaves the exposure unknown; (b) A warning does not tell whether the nurse has taken the germ; (c) A move to another ward spreads the risk if the germ has been taken.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a warning looks like the discipline of a manager.

5-Second Recall: TB exposure = pehle staff ka test, phir baaki sab.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every exposure of the staff is treated first as a health matter.

question: A nurse reads the culture report of a 60-year-old woman on the ward and sees that the germ answers only to a drug kept for the last resort. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Send another culture from the same site the same day
option_2: Double the dose of the usual drug and watch the report again
option_3: Confirm the order with the doctor and start strict contact precautions
option_4: Take the woman off every drug and wait for the fever to decide
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Confirm the order with the doctor and start strict contact precautions

Clinical Rationale: The order is confirmed with the doctor and contact precautions are begun at once, because a germ that answers only to a drug of the last resort spreads on the hands and the articles of the ward faster than any other.

Key Clue: culture report of a 60-year-old woman on the ward with a germ that answers only to a drug of the last resort

Priority Principle: Infection control / Resistant germ

Why Not Others: (a) A second culture delays the precautions that stop the spread; (b) A doubled dose of a drug the germ does not fear is no drug at all; (d) A wait without any drug lets the infection reach the blood.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a bigger dose looks like the stronger answer of a worried nurse.

5-Second Recall: Last-resort germ = doctor confirm karo, contact precautions turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: A resistant germ is fought with barriers before it is fought with drugs.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse must teach a family the care of the linen of a 55-year-old man on contact precautions at home. Which advice is the MOST important for the nurse to give?
option_1: Wash the linen of the man separately in hot water with soap and dry it in the sun
option_2: Soak the linen of the whole family together in cold water overnight
option_3: Give the linen of the man to the dhobi with the other clothes
option_4: Boil every cloth of the house twice a day
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wash the linen of the man separately in hot water with soap and dry it in the sun

Clinical Rationale: The linen of the man is washed separately in hot water with soap and dried in the sun, because the sun and the heat kill the germs that cold water and a shared wash spread.

Key Clue: family of a 55-year-old man on contact precautions learning the care of the linen at home

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Linen at home

Why Not Others: (b) A shared soak passes the germs of the man to every cloth of the house; (c) A dhobi washes the clothes of many houses in one place; (d) Boiling every cloth twice a day wastes fuel and is not needed.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because an overnight soak looks like the deep clean of an old home.

5-Second Recall: Patient ka linen alag, garam paani + dhoop me sukhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The sun is the cheapest disinfectant of an Indian home.

question: A 60-year-old man with diabetes comes to the clinic with a wound on the foot that has been discharging pus for a week, and the flesh at the edge looks black. Which action has the HIGHEST priority?
option_1: Take the weight and the blood pressure for the record
option_2: Give teaching about the sugar and the diet of the man
option_3: Do the dressing with the ointment that the man has been using
option_4: Send the man for a test of the wound and inform the doctor about the black flesh at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Send the man for a test of the wound and inform the doctor about the black flesh at once

Clinical Rationale: A wound of the foot with pus and black flesh in a man with diabetes may be gangrene that can cost the foot, so the test and the doctor come before any teaching or record.

Key Clue: 60-year-old man with diabetes at the clinic with a wound of the foot discharging pus and black flesh at the edge

Priority Principle: Safety / Wound of the foot

Why Not Others: (a) A record of the weight does not save a dying foot; (b) The teaching of the diet is needed and comes after the wound is safe; (c) The old ointment has already failed for a week.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the diet is the long-term care of diabetes.

5-Second Recall: Sugar + kaala ghav = gangrene, turant doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Black flesh on a foot with diabetes is an emergency of hours.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse finds a 30-year-old woman on the ward who has a mental illness washing her hands until the skin bleeds, and the woman says the germs will kill her family. Which response should the nurse give FIRST?
option_1: You must stop washing now or the skin will be spoilt forever
option_2: Your hands are clean; there are no germs that can kill your family
option_3: I can see how frightened you are; let us sit and use the plan we made for this fear
option_4: I will ask the doctor for a stronger tablet for you today
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) I can see how frightened you are; let us sit and use the plan we made for this fear

Clinical Rationale: The fear is named and the agreed plan of therapy is used, because the fear is the illness and NOT a fact, and a plan holds the woman between the fear and the bleeding skin.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman on the ward washing her hands until the skin bleeds, with a fear of germs that will kill her family

Priority Principle: Psychosocial / Fear of germs

Why Not Others: (a) A warning of the spoilt skin feeds the same fear of harm; (b) A fact against a fear of this depth does not touch it; (d) A tablet may come later and is not the first response of the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a fact looks like the simple cure of a wrong belief.

5-Second Recall: Compulsion se bleeding = dar ko naam do, plan lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The nurse answers the fear first and the hands second.

question: A community health nurse visits the home of a 25-year-old mother who has a fresh cut on her hand from cleaning the drain of the yard. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Put turmeric on the cut and tie it with a clean cloth
option_2: Wash the wound with clean water and soap and ask about the last tetanus injection
option_3: Ask the mother to rest the hand and come to the clinic if it pains
option_4: Give a tablet against the germs from the stock of the sub-centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Wash the wound with clean water and soap and ask about the last tetanus injection

Clinical Rationale: A cut from a drain is washed with clean water and soap and the record of the tetanus injection is checked, because the drain carries the germ of lockjaw and the wound is the door it enters by.

Key Clue: 25-year-old mother at home with a fresh cut on the hand from cleaning the drain of the yard

Priority Principle: First aid / Cut of the hand

Why Not Others: (a) Turmeric is a custom and not a clean of a drain wound; (c) A wait for the pain lets the germ of lockjaw settle in; (d) A tablet against the germs is not the protection against lockjaw.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a tablet looks like the whole treatment of a wound.

5-Second Recall: Drain ka cut = paani-sabun se dhoyo, TT yaad karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every wound of the soil and the drain asks the date of the last tetanus injection.

question: A 2-year-old child on the ward with an infection of the chest is to receive a drug against the germs through a line in the hand. Which action is the MOST important to protect the line from infection?
option_1: Cover the site of the line with a thick bandage changed once a day
option_2: Wash the hands and clean the port of the line before every use of it
option_3: Give the drug fast so that the line is open for a shorter time
option_4: Let the mother hold the child during the drug and touch the line freely
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Wash the hands and clean the port of the line before every use of it

Clinical Rationale: The hands are washed and the port is cleaned before every use, because the line is a door into the blood and every touch of a dirty hand or port is a chance for germs.

Key Clue: 2-year-old child on the ward with a line in the hand for a drug against the germs

Priority Principle: Infection control / Line of the child

Why Not Others: (a) A thick bandage hides the early signs of an infection of the site; (c) A fast drug can harm the vein and does not keep the line clean; (d) A free touch of the line by any hand carries the germs in.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a bandage looks like the cover that keeps the germs out.

5-Second Recall: IV port har baar saaf karo - haath dhone ke baad.

PNC Exam Pearl: The line is cleaned at every use and looked at every shift.

question: A nurse on the morning round on the ward finds a client's dressing trolley uncovered, with the sterile packs open beside it. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Use the packs that look dry and untouched for the FIRST dressings
option_2: Cover the trolley with a fresh cloth and use the packs for the morning dressings
option_3: Remove the open packs from use and have the trolley re-set with fresh sterile articles
option_4: Ask the aide who set the trolley to cover it quickly
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Remove the open packs from use and have the trolley re-set with fresh sterile articles

Clinical Rationale: The open packs are removed from use and the trolley is re-set, because a sterile article left uncovered in the open air of the ward is spoilt no matter how dry or untouched it looks.

Key Clue: dressing trolley found uncovered with the sterile packs open

Priority Principle: Infection control / Sterile trolley

Why Not Others: (a) Dryness is not the test of sterility and a look cannot see the germs; (b) A cloth over the spoilt packs does not make them sterile again; (d) A quick cover by the aide agrees that the packs were never spoilt.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a covered trolley looks like the safe trolley of the ward.

5-Second Recall: Khula sterile pack = barbaad, naya set karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sterility is never judged by the eye.

question: A nurse notes that the pads of a 24-year-old woman on the ward who is two days after a birth have a foul smell, and the fever of the woman is rising. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Teach the woman the cleaning of the pads for the days at home
option_2: Change the pad more often and record the smell in the chart
option_3: Give a hot fomentation over the lower belly of the woman
option_4: Inform the doctor and prepare to send a sample of the discharge for a culture
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Inform the doctor and prepare to send a sample of the discharge for a culture

Clinical Rationale: A foul smell of the pads with a rising fever after a birth points to an infection of the womb, so the doctor is told and a culture of the discharge is prepared.

Key Clue: 24-year-old woman on the ward two days after a birth with foul-smelling pads and a rising fever

Priority Principle: Safety / Infection after the birth

Why Not Others: (a) Teaching for the home comes when the infection is treated; (b) A change of the pad does not touch the infection of the womb; (c) A hot fomentation on an infected womb brings more blood to the germs.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a change of the pad looks like the clean answer to a smell.

5-Second Recall: Puerperal sepsis = badbu + bukhar, culture bhejo, doctor bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The smell of the pads after a birth is never a small sign.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse is to give a bed bath to a 70-year-old man on the ward who is on contact precautions. Which set of articles is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take into the room?
option_1: All the articles of the bath at once, so that the nurse need NOT leave the room
option_2: The basin and the soap FIRST, and fetch the rest as needed
option_3: The chart, the phone and the basin so that the notes are made inside
option_4: No articles at all, since the bathroom of the ward has everything
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) All the articles of the bath at once, so that the nurse need NOT leave the room

Clinical Rationale: Every article of the bath goes in at once, because the nurse on contact precautions must NOT leave and re-enter the room and carry the germs out on the uniform.

Key Clue: bed bath of a 70-year-old man on the ward on contact precautions

Priority Principle: Infection control / Articles of the room

Why Not Others: (b) Fetching as needed means many trips in and out of the room; (c) The chart and the phone take the germs of the room to the desk; (d) A bathroom shared by the ward cannot be used on precautions.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because fetching as needed is the habit of an ordinary bath.

5-Second Recall: Contact precaution me saara saaman ek baar me andar.

PNC Exam Pearl: What goes into the room stays there till the care is over.

question: A nurse reads the stool report of a 5-year-old child on the ward who has loose stools with blood, and sees a germ of the rod family with a red colour under the stain. Which germ is the MOST likely?
option_1: A germ of the acid-fast family that causes an illness of the lungs
option_2: A germ of the cluster family that causes a boil of the skin
option_3: A germ of the chain family that causes a sore throat
option_4: A germ of the rod family of the gut that causes a bloody loose stool
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A germ of the rod family of the gut that causes a bloody loose stool

Clinical Rationale: A rod of the gut with a red colour under the stain that causes loose stools with blood is one of the germs of dysentery of the gut.

Key Clue: stool report of a 5-year-old child on the ward with loose stools and blood showing a red rod

Priority Principle: Lab / Germ of the stool

Why Not Others: (a) The acid-fast family causes an illness of the lungs and not of the stool; (b) The cluster family lives on the skin and not in the stool; (c) The chain family causes a sore throat and not a stool of blood.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the cluster germ is the FIRST germ every nurse learns.

5-Second Recall: Khooni loose motion = gut ka red rod, dysentery ka germ.

PNC Exam Pearl: A red rod in a stool of blood is a germ of dysentery.

question: A nurse must collect a blood sample from a 45-year-old man on the ward for a culture, while he has a fever with chills. Which time is the BEST for the nurse to choose?
option_1: At any time of the day, as the germs are always in the blood
option_2: Two hours after the tablet for the fever has been given
option_3: As close to the chill as possible, when the germs are MOST likely in the blood
option_4: Just before the night meal, so that the man is fasting
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) As close to the chill as possible, when the germs are MOST likely in the blood

Clinical Rationale: The chill of a fever is the moment when the germs are MOST often poured into the blood, so the culture is drawn as close to the chill as possible.

Key Clue: blood sample from a 45-year-old man on the ward for a culture during a fever with chills

Priority Principle: Lab / Time of the culture

Why Not Others: (a) The germs come in waves and are not always in the blood; (b) A tablet for the fever cools the skin and does not clear the germs from the blood; (d) A fasting state has nothing to do with a culture of the blood.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a time after the tablet looks like an ordered and quiet hour.

5-Second Recall: Blood culture = chill ke waqt ke paas lo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The chill is the alarm clock of the culture.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse reads the blood report of a 30-year-old woman on the ward who has a fever and sees a rise of the white cells that fight germs of the worm family. Which condition is the MOST likely?
option_1: A heavy loss of blood in the woman
option_2: An infection of worms of the gut or an illness of allergy
option_3: An infection of a bacterial kind in the blood
option_4: A cancer of the marrow of the bones
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) An infection of worms of the gut or an illness of allergy

Clinical Rationale: A rise of the white cells that fight worms points to an infection of worms of the gut or to an illness of allergy, which are the two common causes of that rise.

Key Clue: blood report of a 30-year-old woman on the ward with a fever and a rise of the cells that fight worms

Priority Principle: Lab / Kinds of the white cells

Why Not Others: (a) A loss of blood shows in the red cells and the iron; (c) A bacterial infection raises another kind of the white cells; (d) A cancer of the marrow shows young and strange cells of every kind.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a bacterial infection is the commonest fever of a ward.

5-Second Recall: Eosinophil badhna = keede ya allergy.

PNC Exam Pearl: Each kind of the white cell tells its own story.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse manager on the ward plans the roster during an outbreak of an infection of the gut that has spread from one client to another. Which duty is the MOST important for the manager to give?
option_1: Assign fixed nurses to the infected clients and fixed nurses to the others
option_2: Let every nurse give care to every client so that all learn the care
option_3: Reduce the number of nurses so that fewer hands carry the germs
option_4: Give the new nurses the infected clients as a part of the training
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Assign fixed nurses to the infected clients and fixed nurses to the others

Clinical Rationale: Fixed nurses for the infected clients and fixed nurses for the others stop the germs travelling on the hands and the uniform from one group to the other, which is the main work of a roster in an outbreak.

Key Clue: roster on the ward during an outbreak of an infection of the gut that has spread from one client to another

Priority Principle: Management / Cohort nursing

Why Not Others: (b) A mixed care carries the germs of every infected client to every other; (c) Fewer hands mean more tired hands and more mistakes; (d) New nurses learn best away from the heart of an outbreak.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a mixed care looks like the fair sharing of a hard load.

5-Second Recall: Outbreak me cohort nursing - infected aur non-infected alag nurses.

PNC Exam Pearl: The roster is a barrier as real as the gown.

question: A 50-year-old woman on the ward who has taken a drug against the germs for a week now has white patches in the mouth that come off when rubbed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Ask the woman to gargle with salt water three times a day
option_2: Inform the doctor about the patches, which are a growth of yeast
option_3: Give the woman a tablet against the germs of a different kind
option_4: Tell the woman to brush the patches off with the toothbrush
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Inform the doctor about the patches, which are a growth of yeast

Clinical Rationale: White patches that come off when rubbed during a course of a drug against the germs are a growth of yeast that has taken the place of the normal germs the drug killed, so the doctor is told.

Key Clue: 50-year-old woman on the ward given a drug against the germs for a week with white patches in the mouth

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Yeast of the mouth

Why Not Others: (a) A gargle of salt water does not treat a growth of yeast; (c) A nurse does not choose a drug against the germs herself; (d) A brush over the patches makes sore places that the yeast enters.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a gargle looks like the home cure of every mouth.

5-Second Recall: Antibiotic ke baad mouth ke safed daag = fungal infection, doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The drug that kills the bad germs can open the door to the yeast.

question: A nurse must dispose of the gloves and the gown after the care of a 40-year-old man on the ward who is on contact precautions. Which order of removal is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The gloves FIRST, then wash the hands, then the gown
option_2: The gown FIRST, then the gloves, then the hands
option_3: Both together, pulled from the shoulders and dropped on the floor
option_4: Wash the hands over the gloves, then take both off together
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The gloves FIRST, then wash the hands, then the gown

Clinical Rationale: The gloves come off FIRST because they hold the heaviest load of germs, the hands are washed, and then the gown comes off without the clean hands touching the soiled front.

Key Clue: disposal of the gloves and the gown after the care of a 40-year-old man on the ward on contact precautions

Priority Principle: Infection control / Order of removal

Why Not Others: (b) A gown taken off over soiled gloves soils the uniform and the hands; (c) Articles dropped on the floor carry the germs to the shoes; (d) A wash over the gloves is a wash of the gloves and not of the hands.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the gown looks like the outermost thing to come off FIRST.

5-Second Recall: Gloves pehle utaro, haath dhoyo, phir gown.

PNC Exam Pearl: The heaviest germs come off first.

question: A community health nurse reads the report of the water of a well in a village where a mother draws the drinking water, and finds a germ of the rod family that lives in the gut of man. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give tablets against the germs to the whole village now
option_2: Close the well and ask the village to dig a new one at once
option_3: Tell the village the water is safe, as no one has fallen ill yet
option_4: Advise the village to boil the water before every drink and report the finding
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Advise the village to boil the water before every drink and report the finding

Clinical Rationale: The water is boiled before every drink and the finding is reported, so that every family is guarded the same day while the source is treated.

Key Clue: report of the water of a well in a village with a germ of the gut

Priority Principle: Community / Safe water

Why Not Others: (a) Tablets for a whole village breed resistance and do not clean the well; (b) A new well takes months and leaves the village unguarded today; (c) No illness yet does not make a found germ safe.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a closed well looks like the sure end of the danger.

5-Second Recall: Well me gut germ = paani ubaal ke piyo, report karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Boiling guards the family today while the well is treated.

question: A nurse is teaching a student the five moments of hand washing of the WHO. Which moment is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to use for a 60-year-old man on the ward with a line in the vein?
option_1: When the hands look soiled to the eye
option_2: After the care of the whole body of the man and at no other time
option_3: Before and after touching the line or the site of the line
option_4: Before the meal of the man and after the bed is made
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Before and after touching the line or the site of the line

Clinical Rationale: The line goes into the vein of the man, so the hands are washed before and after every touch of the line or its site, which is one of the five moments named for the safety of the blood.

Key Clue: teaching of the five moments of hand washing for a 60-year-old man on the ward with a line in the vein

Priority Principle: Infection control / Five moments

Why Not Others: (a) The eye cannot see the germs that the hands carry; (b) A wash after the care does not guard the man during it; (d) The meal and the bed are moments of comfort and not of the line.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because washing after the care is the habit MOST deeply set.

5-Second Recall: IV line chhue se pehle aur baad - dono baar haath.

PNC Exam Pearl: The line is touched with clean hands or not at all.

question: A nurse must clean the wounds of a man and a woman who share a room on the ward, one with a clean wound and one with an infected wound of pus. Which order of care is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The clean wound FIRST and the infected wound last, with a wash of the hands between
option_2: The infected wound FIRST so that the pus is cleared before the clean wound
option_3: Both wounds with the same pair of gloves to save the stock
option_4: The order does NOT matter if the dressings are changed by two nurses
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The clean wound FIRST and the infected wound last, with a wash of the hands between

Clinical Rationale: The clean wound is cared for FIRST and the infected wound last with a wash of the hands between, so that the germs of the pus never travel to the wound that has none.

Key Clue: a man and a woman who share a room on the ward, one with a clean wound and one with an infected wound of pus

Priority Principle: Infection control / Order of the care

Why Not Others: (b) A pus first carries its germs on everything to the clean wound; (c) One pair of gloves between two wounds is one wound infecting the other; (d) Two nurses with a wrong order share the germs at the trolley.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the infected wound looks like the urgent one of the two.

5-Second Recall: Clean pehle, infected baad me - ye order kabhi na badlo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The care moves from the cleanest to the dirtiest.

question: A nurse notes that the germ grown from the wound of a 55-year-old man on the ward does NOT answer to the FIRST drug against the germs. Which term is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to use for this finding?
option_1: The man has an allergy to that drug
option_2: The germ has died inside the wound
option_3: The sample was taken from the wrong site
option_4: The germ has become resistant to that drug
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The germ has become resistant to that drug

Clinical Rationale: A germ that does NOT answer to a drug it once feared has become resistant to it, which is read from the list of drugs on the culture report.

Key Clue: germ grown from the wound of a 55-year-old man on the ward that does NOT answer to the FIRST drug

Priority Principle: Lab / Resistance

Why Not Others: (a) An allergy is a reaction of the body and not of the germ; (b) A germ that grows on the dish is alive and not dead; (c) A wrong site would show a different germ and not a resistant one.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a grown germ is often read as a beaten germ.

5-Second Recall: Drug kaam na kare = resistance, report ki list dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The list on the report tells which drugs the germ still fears.

question: A nurse reads the sputum report of a 50-year-old man on the ward and sees the words 'resistant to the drugs of the FIRST line'. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the man the illness is now beyond any treatment
option_2: Repeat the test of the sputum at once from a fresh sample
option_3: Inform the doctor and begin teaching the long course of the second-line drugs
option_4: Continue the FIRST-line drugs and wait for a better report
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Inform the doctor and begin teaching the long course of the second-line drugs

Clinical Rationale: A resistance to the drugs of the FIRST line means the illness needs the long course of the second-line drugs under the care of the doctor, and the teaching of the man begins the same day because a course of two years is finished only by a man who understands it.

Key Clue: sputum report of a 50-year-old man on the ward with resistance to the drugs of the FIRST line

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Resistant tuberculosis

Why Not Others: (a) A word of despair is false and takes away the hope that the treatment needs; (b) A repeat sample delays a treatment that the report has already settled; (d) Drugs the germ no longer fears only teach it to fear nothing.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a repeat test looks like the careful step of a doubt.

5-Second Recall: MDR-TB = second-line drugs ka lamba course, teaching aaj se.

PNC Exam Pearl: The resistant illness is treated with hope and with the full course.

question: A nurse must collect a sample from the wound of a 65-year-old woman on the ward for a culture of a germ that grows only when air is absent. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Swab the surface of the wound with the usual cotton swab
option_2: Take the sample from deep in the wound with a syringe and push out the air at once
option_3: Leave the swab open in the air for a minute before it goes into the tube
option_4: Collect the sample and keep the tube open so that the germ has air to live
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Take the sample from deep in the wound with a syringe and push out the air at once

Clinical Rationale: A germ that grows without air dies in the air, so the sample is drawn from deep in the wound by a syringe and the air of the syringe is pushed out at once so that the germ reaches the laboratory alive.

Key Clue: sample from the wound of a 65-year-old woman on the ward for a germ that grows only when air is absent

Priority Principle: Procedure / Anaerobic sample

Why Not Others: (a) A surface swab collects the germs of the air and of the skin; (c) A minute in the air begins the death of the germ; (d) An open tube is a door for the very air that kills the germ.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the swab is the tool of every ordinary wound.

5-Second Recall: Anaerobic culture = gehraai se syringe se lo, hawa nikal do.

PNC Exam Pearl: The germ that grows without air is carried in a closed world of its own.

question: A nurse manager on the ward reads the monthly report of the infections and sees a rise of the infections of the urinary tract, MOST often in a man with a catheter. Which action should the manager take FIRST?
option_1: Call a meeting of the ward and re-teach the care of the catheters with a daily checklist
option_2: Order more catheters of a new kind for the whole ward
option_3: Stop the use of catheters in the ward until the numbers fall
option_4: Ask the doctor of each client to remove the catheter that week
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Call a meeting of the ward and re-teach the care of the catheters with a daily checklist

Clinical Rationale: A rise of catheter infections is met FIRST by re-teaching the care of the catheters with a checklist, because the commonest cause is a break in technique that a shared review finds and mends.

Key Clue: monthly report of the ward with a rise of the infections of the urinary tract, MOST often in a man with a catheter

Priority Principle: Management / Rise of an infection

Why Not Others: (b) New catheters do not mend a break in the technique of the hands; (c) The catheters are needed by the clients and cannot simply stop; (d) A nurse manager raises the finding with the team and does not order the doctors.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because new equipment looks like the modern answer of a manager.

5-Second Recall: Catheter UTI badha = team meeting + checklist.

PNC Exam Pearl: The manager mends the technique before the stock.

question: A nurse is to carry the soiled linen of a 50-year-old man on the ward who is on contact precautions to the laundry. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Shake the linen in the room so that the dust falls there and NOT outside
option_2: Roll the linen without shaking and carry it in a bag that does NOT let water through
option_3: Sort the linen of the man with the linen of the others at the door
option_4: Carry the linen in the arms, wrapped in the sheet of the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Roll the linen without shaking and carry it in a bag that does NOT let water through

Clinical Rationale: The linen is rolled without shaking and carried in a bag that holds the wet, because a shake throws the germs into the air and an open carrying spreads them along the corridor.

Key Clue: soiled linen of a 50-year-old man on the ward on contact precautions to be carried to the laundry

Priority Principle: Infection control / Soiled linen

Why Not Others: (a) A shake in the room fills the air of the room with germs; (c) A sort at the door mixes the linen of the man with the clean loads; (d) Linen carried in the arms wets the uniform of the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because shaking indoors looks like keeping the dirt in one place.

5-Second Recall: Gandi chadar hilaaye bina roll karo, leak-proof bag me bhejo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The germs of the linen travel on the air of a shake.

question: A community health nurse visits the village to plan a camp where a mother learns how to protect her child from an illness that spreads through the air. Which method of teaching should carry the MOST weight?
option_1: A poster on the wall of the panchayat office
option_2: A long lecture on the germs and their names in the book
option_3: A short talk with a demonstration of covering the mouth and washing the hands
option_4: A pamphlet in the language of the district given to the head of each house
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A short talk with a demonstration of covering the mouth and washing the hands

Clinical Rationale: A short talk with a demonstration lets the village see and copy the two acts that stop the spread - the covered mouth and the washed hands - which a lecture or a paper cannot teach.

Key Clue: camp to teach a village about an illness that spreads through the air

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Method of the camp

Why Not Others: (a) A poster teaches only those who stop and read; (b) The names of the germs do not change the acts of the village; (d) A pamphlet with the head of the house may never reach the hands.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a lecture looks like the serious teaching of a school.

5-Second Recall: Village camp = chhoti baat + demonstration, lamba lecture nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The teaching that is seen is the teaching that is done.

question: A nurse reads the blood report of a 28-year-old woman on the ward who has had a fever for two weeks, and sees that the germ grows only on a special medium of the bile. Which germ is the MOST likely?
option_1: The germ of the lung that grows in eight weeks on a special egg medium
option_2: The germ of the boil that grows on any dish of blood
option_3: The germ of the throat that grows in a day on the usual medium
option_4: The germ of enteric fever that lives in the bile of the gall bladder
solution:
