Correct Answer: (d) The germ of enteric fever that lives in the bile of the gall bladder

Clinical Rationale: A germ that grows only on a medium of bile in a fever of two weeks is the germ of enteric fever, which lives in the bile and is grown on media that hold it.

Key Clue: blood report of a 28-year-old woman on the ward with a fever for two weeks and a germ grown on a medium of bile

Priority Principle: Lab / Germ of the bile

Why Not Others: (a) The germ of the lung takes eight weeks and grows on an egg medium; (b) The germ of a boil grows easily and is not picky about the medium; (c) The germ of the throat grows in a day without a special medium.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the germ of the lung is the famous slow grower of the laboratory.

5-Second Recall: Do hafte ka bukhar + bile medium = typhoid ka germ.

PNC Exam Pearl: The bile medium is the home of the germ of enteric fever.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse must give a bedpan to a 70-year-old woman on the ward who is on contact precautions. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wear the same gloves to give the bedpan and to open the door of the room
option_2: Place the bedpan and leave the room until the woman calls
option_3: Place the paper cover on the bedpan and keep the articles for hand hygiene within reach
option_4: Ask the woman to hold her need until the shift of the nurse is over
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Place the paper cover on the bedpan and keep the articles for hand hygiene within reach

Clinical Rationale: The paper cover is placed and the means of cleaning the hands are kept within reach, so that the care is given and the hands are cleaned before any touch of the door or the chart.

Key Clue: bedpan for a 70-year-old woman on the ward on contact precautions

Priority Principle: Infection control / Care of the bedpan

Why Not Others: (a) The same gloves on the woman and the door carry the germs out; (b) A nurse who leaves the room first cleans nothing on the way; (d) A need held for hours harms the bladder and the dignity of the woman.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because leaving the room looks like respect for privacy.

5-Second Recall: Bedpan ke baad gloves utaro, haath dhoyo, phir darwaza.

PNC Exam Pearl: The door of the room is touched only with clean hands.

question: A nurse reads the report of a 40-year-old man on the ward and sees a rise of the cells that carry oxygen and a thickening of the blood. Which condition is the MOST likely?
option_1: A cancer of the marrow of the bones
option_2: A heavy bleeding in the last hours
option_3: An infection of the blood of a bacterial kind
option_4: A lack of water in the body that has thickened the blood
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A lack of water in the body that has thickened the blood

Clinical Rationale: A rise of the cells that carry oxygen with a thick blood is the picture of a body short of water, where the same cells float in less plasma and the report reads high.

Key Clue: report of a 40-year-old man on the ward with a rise of the oxygen-carrying cells and a thick blood

Priority Principle: Lab / Thick blood

Why Not Others: (a) A cancer of the marrow shows strange young cells of every line; (b) A bleeding thins the count of the cells and never raises it; (c) An infection raises the white cells and not the oxygen carriers.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because bleeding is the fear behind every blood report.

5-Second Recall: RBC high + thick blood = paani ki kami.

PNC Exam Pearl: The blood reads thick when the water of the body runs low.

question: A 30-year-old woman on the ward is given a drug against the germs and asks the nurse whether she must finish it even though she feels well on the third day. Which reply is the BEST that the nurse can give?
option_1: Yes, finish the full course, because stopping early breeds germs that resist the drug
option_2: No, stop when you feel well, because the body needs no more drug
option_3: Take the tablets on the days the fever returns
option_4: Give the remaining tablets to a family member with the same illness
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Yes, finish the full course, because stopping early breeds germs that resist the drug

Clinical Rationale: The full course is finished, because the germs that survive an early stop grow strong against the drug and the illness returns in a form no drug of that group can touch.

Key Clue: 30-year-old woman on the ward given a drug against the germs who feels well on the third day

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Full course

Why Not Others: (b) Feeling well means the drug is winning and not that the war is over; (c) Tablets taken on the off days teach the germs the most; (d) Leftover drugs are never the drug for the illness of another person.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the feel of wellness looks like the proof of the cure.

5-Second Recall: Tablet feel good = course poora karo, adhoora chhodo mat.

PNC Exam Pearl: A full course is the cheapest protection against resistance.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse in the labour room notes that the instruments used for the birth of a 28-year-old woman and her baby were boiled in water that never rolled. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Record the lapse in the chart and carry on with the usual care
option_2: Treat the birth as a risk of infection and inform the doctor to plan the protection of the mother and the baby
option_3: Re-boil a fresh set of instruments for the next birth
option_4: Ask the aide who boiled the water to write an apology
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Treat the birth as a risk of infection and inform the doctor to plan the protection of the mother and the baby

Clinical Rationale: Water that never rolled has NOT sterilised the instruments, so the birth is treated as a risk and the doctor plans the protection of the mother and the baby against the infection that may follow.

Key Clue: instruments boiled in water that never rolled, used for the birth of a 28-year-old woman

Priority Principle: Safety / Sterilisation of the birth

Why Not Others: (a) A record does not protect the mother or the baby from the germs; (c) Fresh instruments help the next woman and not this one; (d) An apology is not the care of an exposed birth.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a record looks like the whole duty of the finding.

5-Second Recall: Ubalta paani jo ubla nahi = sterilisation fail, doctor ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Water must roll before it can be called boiling.

question: A nurse is about to change the dressing of a surgical wound on a 45-year-old man on the ward. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the wound with normal saline before washing the hands
option_2: Put on sterile gloves and open the sterile pack at once
option_3: Wash the hands and clean the trolley before touching the sterile pack
option_4: Ask the man to turn on his side and uncover the wound
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Wash the hands and clean the trolley before touching the sterile pack

Clinical Rationale: Clean hands are the FIRST step of every aseptic procedure, and the trolley is cleaned before the sterile pack is opened so that the field stays free of germs.

Key Clue: dressing change of a surgical wound on a 45-year-old man on the ward

Priority Principle: Infection control / Aseptic technique

Why Not Others: (a) A wound cleaned with unclean hands takes the germs of the hands into it; (b) Sterile gloves over unclean hands are spoiled gloves; (d) Positioning comes after the nurse is ready and the field is clean.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because sterile gloves look like the start of a sterile procedure.

5-Second Recall: Aseptic dressing se pehle haath dhoyo aur trolley saaf karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands come before sterile gloves.

question: A nurse manager on the ward must assign the care of a 60-year-old client on contact precautions for an infection of the gut. Which task can BEST be assigned to a nursing assistant?
option_1: Deciding when the precautions may be stopped
option_2: Teaching the client about the spread of the infection
option_3: Assessing the skin of the client for signs of dehydration
option_4: Bathing the client and changing the bed linen with the gloves and gown
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Bathing the client and changing the bed linen with the gloves and gown

Clinical Rationale: Bathing and changing the linen are routine tasks that a nursing assistant can do with the gloves and gown, while teaching, assessing and deciding on precautions need the judgement of a registered nurse.

Key Clue: care of a 60-year-old client on the ward on contact precautions for an infection of the gut

Priority Principle: Management / Delegation

Why Not Others: (a) Deciding on the precautions is the duty of the nurse and the doctor; (b) Teaching needs the knowledge and the licence of a registered nurse; (c) Assessment of the skin is a nursing judgement and not a task to hand over.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because looking at the skin looks like a simple task.

5-Second Recall: Contact precaution me bathing/linen assistant ko, teaching-assessment nurse.

PNC Exam Pearl: A task is delegated by its risk and not by its look.

question: A nurse cares for a 55-year-old man on the ward who has a central line in the neck for fluids. Which finding should the nurse report to the doctor FIRST?
option_1: Redness and a discharge at the line site with a new fever
option_2: A slight complaint of cold at the site of the line
option_3: A record of the dressing changed two days ago
option_4: A small air bubble in the tubing of the line
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Redness and a discharge at the line site with a new fever

Clinical Rationale: Redness, a discharge and a new fever at the site of a central line are the early signs of a line infection, which is reported at once because the line reaches the bloodstream.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man on the ward with a central line in the neck, now with redness and discharge at the site and a new fever

Priority Principle: Safety / Central line infection

Why Not Others: (b) A feeling of cold at the site is not the sign of an infection; (c) A dressing changed two days ago is the usual practice; (d) A small air bubble in the tubing is common and not the first danger.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the complaint of cold looks like the FIRST change to report.

5-Second Recall: Central line site pe laali + discharge + bukhar = line infection, turant batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The line that reaches the heart can carry the germ there in hours.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A community health nurse visits the village where five children have fever with a rash within a week, and a mother reports that one child also has a cough and red eyes. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the vaccine to the children who are still healthy
option_2: Inform the medical officer and begin the search for the other cases in the village
option_3: Advise the families to keep the children indoors for a week
option_4: Send a report at the end of the month with the other cases
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Inform the medical officer and begin the search for the other cases in the village

Clinical Rationale: A cluster of fever with a rash, cough and red eyes in one village suggests an outbreak of a notified disease, so the medical officer is informed and the search for other cases begins at once.

Key Clue: five children in one village with fever and a rash within a week, two with a cough and red eyes

Priority Principle: Community / Outbreak

Why Not Others: (a) A vaccine given after exposure may help some and is not the first step; (c) Keeping children indoors limits spread but does not begin the watch; (d) A monthly report is far too late for an outbreak that grows by the week.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a vaccine looks like the sure answer to a rash.

5-Second Recall: Ek gaon me 5 bachche fever+rash = outbreak, MO ko batao, case search.

PNC Exam Pearl: An outbreak is an event of hours and not of a month.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse manager on the ward teaches a group of new staff the single practice that protects every client and every nurse. Which practice is the MOST important for the manager to name?
option_1: Clean the equipment of the ward at the end of every shift
option_2: Wear a full set of barriers for every client of the ward
option_3: Keep a client with an infection at the far end of the ward
option_4: Treat every client's blood and body fluids as if they may carry an infection
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Treat every client's blood and body fluids as if they may carry an infection

Clinical Rationale: Treating every client's blood and body fluids as possibly infectious is the single practice of standard precautions that protects both the client and the nurse in every care.

Key Clue: teaching a group of new staff the single practice that protects every client and every nurse

Priority Principle: Management / Standard precautions

Why Not Others: (a) Cleaning the equipment at the end of a shift misses every care in between; (b) A full set of barriers for every care is neither needed nor practical; (c) Keeping a client at a distance does not follow the way an illness spreads.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because more barriers look like more safety.

5-Second Recall: Standard precaution = har client ka blood/fluid infectious maano.

PNC Exam Pearl: Standard precautions are used for every client, known infection or not.

question: A nurse must prepare articles for sterilisation in the autoclave after the care of a client on the ward. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the articles of all visible dirt and dry them before they are packed
option_2: Pack the articles tight together so that the steam reaches more of them
option_3: Add a little water to the articles so that they stay moist in the steam
option_4: Seal the packs air-tight so that the steam does NOT enter them
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the articles of all visible dirt and dry them before they are packed

Clinical Rationale: Articles are cleaned of all visible dirt and dried before packing, because the steam of the autoclave cannot kill the germs that lie under a coat of dirt or blood.

Key Clue: articles to be sterilised in the autoclave of the ward

Priority Principle: Infection control / Sterilisation

Why Not Others: (b) Articles packed tight stop the steam from reaching their surfaces; (c) Extra water inside a pack keeps the steam out of the cloth; (d) An air-tight seal gives the steam no way into the pack.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a tight pack looks like a strong pack.

5-Second Recall: Autoclave se pehle saaman saaf karke sukhao, phir pack karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sterilisation begins with a clean article.

question: A nurse cares for a 65-year-old man on the ward who is on a ventilator and notes a new fever with thick secretions. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give more humidified oxygen through the line
option_2: Suction the secretions with clean technique and inform the doctor
option_3: Change the position of the man every hour
option_4: Loosen the tube and note the amount of the secretions
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Suction the secretions with clean technique and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A new fever with thick secretions in a man on a ventilator suggests an infection of the lungs, so the secretions are cleared with clean technique and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: 65-year-old man on the ward on a ventilator with a new fever and thick secretions

Priority Principle: Safety / Ventilator infection

Why Not Others: (a) More oxygen does not clear the secretions that hold the germs; (c) A change of position helps but does not treat the infection; (d) Loosening the tube risks moving it and does not clear the airway.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because more oxygen looks like the FIRST need of a breathless man.

5-Second Recall: Ventilator + naya bukhar + gehra secretion = VAP, suction karo, doctor batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The ventilator tube is a highway for the germs of the ward.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse reads the culture report of a 50-year-old man on the ward and sees the letters S and R against the list of drugs. Which meaning is the MOST important for the nurse to understand?
option_1: S means the drug is safe and R means the drug is risky
option_2: S means the sample was small and R means the report was repeated
option_3: S means the germ is killed by the drug and R means it resists the drug
option_4: S means the man is sensitive and R means he is resistant to the germ
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) S means the germ is killed by the drug and R means it resists the drug

Clinical Rationale: In a culture report S means the germ is sensitive, that is killed by the drug, and R means the germ is resistant, that is NOT killed by it.

Key Clue: culture report of a 50-year-old man on the ward with the letters S and R against the list of drugs

Priority Principle: Lab / Sensitivity report

Why Not Others: (a) S and R speak of the germ and not of the safety of the drug; (b) S and R have nothing to do with the size of a sample or a repeat; (d) S and R name the germ's response and not the man's state.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because sensitivity sounds like a quality of the person.

5-Second Recall: S = sensitive (dawa kaam karti hai), R = resistant (dawa fail).

PNC Exam Pearl: The report speaks of the germ and not of the man.

question: A 30-year-old man on the ward who has a blood-borne infection asks the nurse NOT to tell his wife or his employer. Which response is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give?
option_1: Keep the report confidential and discuss the testing of the wife with the doctor
option_2: Tell the employer at once so that the workplace is kept safe
option_3: Tell the wife at once without asking the man, as her health comes FIRST
option_4: Record the report in the ward notes that any visitor may read
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the report confidential and discuss the testing of the wife with the doctor

Clinical Rationale: The report of a blood-borne infection is kept confidential, and the wife is offered testing with the counsel of the doctor, because the nurse owes the man privacy and the wife a chance to be protected.

Key Clue: 30-year-old man on the ward with a blood-borne infection asking the nurse NOT to tell his wife or his employer

Priority Principle: Ethics / Confidentiality

Why Not Others: (b) The employer has no right to the report of the man's illness; (c) Telling the wife without the man breaks his privacy and his trust; (d) Ward notes that a visitor may read expose the report to the whole ward.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because the health of the wife looks like the FIRST duty.

5-Second Recall: HIV report confidential rakho, partner ko doctor ke saath testing offer karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Confidentiality is kept and the partner is offered protection in the same care.

question: A 40-year-old man on the ward who is given a drug against the germs now has a rash with swelling of the eyelids after the FIRST dose. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Give the next dose after an hour and watch the rash
option_2: Stop the drug, keep the airway clear and inform the doctor at once
option_3: Note the rash in the chart and continue the drug as ordered
option_4: Apply a soothing lotion on the rash and reassure the man
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the drug, keep the airway clear and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A rash with swelling of the eyelids after the FIRST dose of a drug may be the start of a severe allergic reaction, so the drug is stopped, the airway is kept clear and the doctor is told at once.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man on the ward given a drug against the germs with a rash and swelling of the eyelids after the FIRST dose

Priority Principle: Safety / Drug reaction

Why Not Others: (a) A second dose can turn a mild rash into a dangerous reaction; (c) Noting the rash and going on misses the danger of the swelling; (d) A lotion on the skin does not guard the airway.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because treating the rash looks like the FIRST comfort of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Dawa ke baad rash + eyelid swelling = allergy, drug roko, doctor bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A drug reaction with swelling of the face is treated as an emergency.

question: A nurse must wash the hands at the sink on the ward after the care of a 60-year-old man. Which action is the MOST appropriate method for the nurse to use?
option_1: Use the hand rub when the hands are heavily soiled with blood
option_2: Wash the palms quickly under running water and dry them on the apron
option_3: Rub the hands with soap for at least twenty seconds covering every surface
option_4: Wear gloves while washing so that the soap does NOT touch the skin
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Rub the hands with soap for at least twenty seconds covering every surface

Clinical Rationale: The hands are rubbed with soap for at least twenty seconds over every surface, because the germs of the hands lie between the fingers and under the nails and a quick wash leaves them there.

Key Clue: hand washing by a nurse at the ward sink after the care of a 60-year-old man

Priority Principle: Infection control / Method of hand washing

Why Not Others: (a) Heavily soiled hands need soap and water and not a hand rub; (b) A quick wash of the palms and drying on the apron leaves the germs and adds more; (d) Gloves worn while washing keep the soap off the skin and the germs on.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a quick wash looks like the busy habit of a ward.

5-Second Recall: Haath sabun se 20 second, har surface, phir sukhao.

PNC Exam Pearl: Hand rub for clean hands, soap and water for soiled hands.

question: A nurse reads that a germ from a wound of a 35-year-old man on the ward grows on a medium that turns the colonies a golden colour. Which germ is the MOST likely?
option_1: A germ that grows when air is absent
option_2: A germ of the rod family that lives in the gut
option_3: A germ of the acid-fast family that causes an illness of the lungs
option_4: A germ of the cluster family that causes a boil and a wound of pus
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A germ of the cluster family that causes a boil and a wound of pus

Clinical Rationale: A germ of the cluster family that turns its colonies a golden colour on a medium is the common germ of the skin that causes a boil and a wound of pus.

Key Clue: germ from a wound of a 35-year-old man on the ward grown on a medium that turns the colonies golden

Priority Principle: Lab / Germ of the wound

Why Not Others: (a) A germ that grows without air is seen deep in a wound and is not golden; (b) The rod of the gut does not grow as golden clusters; (c) The acid-fast family grows slowly and causes an illness of the lungs.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the rod of the gut is the commonest germ of the body.

5-Second Recall: Golden colonies = Staphylococcus aureus, pus ka kitanu.

PNC Exam Pearl: Golden colonies on a medium name the common germ of the skin.

question: A nurse teaches the family of a 60-year-old man going home with a germ that resists many drugs. Which advice is the MOST important for the home?
option_1: Use a fresh set of plates and spoons for the man every meal
option_2: Keep the man in a separate room at all times
option_3: Wash the hands with soap before and after every contact with the man
option_4: Boil all the clothes of the house once a week
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Wash the hands with soap before and after every contact with the man

Clinical Rationale: Hand washing before and after every contact is the MOST important advice for a home with a resistant germ, because the hands carry the germ to the other members of the family.

Key Clue: family of a 60-year-old man going home with a germ that resists many drugs

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Resistant germ at home

Why Not Others: (a) Separate plates do not touch the germ that travels on the hands; (b) A separate room for the whole day leaves the care undone and the man alone; (d) Boiling all the clothes weekly misses the moment-to-moment spread.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a separate room looks like the strong guard of an infection.

5-Second Recall: Home me MDRO - sabse zaroori hai haath dhona, alag kamra nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The hands carry the resistant germ between the members of a family.

question: A nurse has collected a blood sample from a 50-year-old man on the ward and must label the tube before it goes to the laboratory. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Label all the tubes together at the desk after the round
option_2: Label the tube at the bedside after checking the name and the identity band of the client
option_3: Ask another nurse to label the tubes from memory
option_4: Write the name of the ward on the tube and send it at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Label the tube at the bedside after checking the name and the identity band of the client

Clinical Rationale: The tube is labelled at the bedside after checking the name against the identity band, so that the sample carries the right name and the report reaches the right client.

Key Clue: blood sample to be labelled before it goes to the laboratory

Priority Principle: Safety / Labelling of the sample

Why Not Others: (a) Tubes labelled at the desk after the round are the way samples get mixed; (c) A label written from memory is the first step of a wrong report; (d) The name of the ward alone does not name the client.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because labelling all the tubes together looks like the fastest way of a busy round.

5-Second Recall: Sample bedside pe label karo, ID band check karke.

PNC Exam Pearl: A tube is labelled beside the client and never at the desk.

question: A nurse on the ward uses an alcohol hand rub after the care of one client and before the care of the next. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Rub the hands until the alcohol has dried completely, covering every surface
option_2: Wipe the hands on the uniform after a quick rub
option_3: Rinse the hands with water after the rub to remove the alcohol
option_4: Use the rub once a shift for the whole round of the ward
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Rub the hands until the alcohol has dried completely, covering every surface

Clinical Rationale: The hands are rubbed until the alcohol dries completely over every surface, because the rub needs its full contact time to kill the germs and a quick rub leaves them alive.

Key Clue: alcohol hand rub used by a nurse after the care of one client and before the care of the next

Priority Principle: Infection control / Hand rub

Why Not Others: (b) Wiping the hands on the uniform puts the germs of the uniform back; (c) Rinsing with water after the rub washes the protection away; (d) A rub once a shift leaves the germs of every client untouched.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because drying the hands on the uniform is the quick habit of a ward.

5-Second Recall: Alcohol rub tab tak ragdo jab tak sukh jaaye.

PNC Exam Pearl: The alcohol rub kills only while it is wet on the hands.

question: A nurse must collect sputum from a 50-year-old man on the ward who is suspected to have tuberculosis. Which sample gives the BEST chance of finding the germ?
option_1: A sample taken from the saliva of the mouth
option_2: A single sample collected after the night meal
option_3: A sample collected after the mouth is rinsed with water
option_4: The early morning sample on three different days
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The early morning sample on three different days

Clinical Rationale: The early morning sample taken on three different days gives the BEST chance, because the germ of tuberculosis is few in the sputum and the overnight sputum holds the MOST of it.

Key Clue: sputum from a 50-year-old man on the ward suspected to have tuberculosis

Priority Principle: Procedure / Sputum for tuberculosis

Why Not Others: (a) Saliva of the mouth comes from the throat and not from the lung; (b) A single sample after a meal holds too few germs to find; (c) A rinse of the mouth washes away the very germs to be found.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because one sample looks like enough for one test.

5-Second Recall: TB ke liye subah ka sputum, teen din, teen sample.

PNC Exam Pearl: The germ of tuberculosis hides in the morning sputum.

question: A nurse must care for the wound of a 50-year-old woman on the ward whose wound is healing with healthy tissue. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Scrub the wound hard to remove all the healthy tissue
option_2: Clean the wound from the dirtiest to the cleanest part
option_3: Use the same gauze for all the parts of the wound
option_4: Clean the wound from the cleanest to the dirtiest part with normal saline
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Clean the wound from the cleanest to the dirtiest part with normal saline

Clinical Rationale: The wound is cleaned from the cleanest to the dirtiest part, so that the germs of the dirtier part are NOT carried back to the part that is healing.

Key Clue: wound of a 50-year-old woman on the ward healing with healthy tissue

Priority Principle: Procedure / Wound care

Why Not Others: (a) Hard scrubbing takes away the healthy tissue the wound needs to heal; (b) Cleaning from the dirtiest to the cleanest carries the germs into the healing part; (c) One gauze for all the parts moves the germs from one part to another.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because starting at the middle of the wound looks like the way of a scrub.

5-Second Recall: Wound saaf se gande ki taraf clean karo, ulta nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: The clean is always finished in the dirtiest place.

question: A nurse teaches the family of a 45-year-old man on the ward who has an infection of the liver that spreads by the stool. Which advice is the MOST important to stop the spread at home?
option_1: Boil the drinking water of the whole house every day
option_2: Give the man a separate room and a separate bathroom
option_3: Wash the hands with soap after touching the man or his used articles
option_4: Keep the children away from the man for one month
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Wash the hands with soap after touching the man or his used articles

Clinical Rationale: Hand washing with soap after touching the man or his used articles stops an infection that leaves the body in the stool, because the hands carry the germ from the man to the food of the family.

Key Clue: family of a 45-year-old man on the ward with an infection of the liver that spreads by the stool

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Spread by the stool

Why Not Others: (a) Boiled water is useful and not the main way this germ travels; (b) A separate room helps little when the hands carry the germ to the food; (d) Children kept a month away still eat with the hands of the house.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a separate room looks like the strong guard of an infection.

5-Second Recall: Hepatitis A - toilet ke baad haath dhona sabse zaroori.

PNC Exam Pearl: An infection of the stool is stopped at the sink.

question: A nurse pours a sterile solution into a bowl on the sterile field of a dressing trolley while caring for a 50-year-old man on the ward. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Hold the bottle close over the field so that no drop is lost
option_2: Hold the bottle away from the field and pour from a height with the label up
option_3: Pour back the extra solution into the bottle for the next use
option_4: Set the cap of the bottle down inside the sterile field
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Hold the bottle away from the field and pour from a height with the label up

Clinical Rationale: The bottle is held away from the field with the label up and the solution poured from a height, so that the edge of the bottle does NOT touch the field and the label is NOT spoiled by the drip.

Key Clue: sterile solution poured into a bowl on the sterile field of a dressing trolley

Priority Principle: Infection control / Sterile field

Why Not Others: (a) A bottle held close over the field may touch it and spoil it; (c) Solution poured back into the bottle carries the germs of the bowl; (d) A cap set down in the field spoils the field at once.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because holding the bottle close looks like the careful way to pour.

5-Second Recall: Sterile solution label upar, bottle field se door, oonchai se daalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: Never reach over a sterile field.

question: A nurse must collect a urine sample from a 2-year-old child on the ward who has a fever, and the child wears a nappy. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Clean the area of the urinary opening and apply a sterile bag to collect the urine
option_2: Collect the urine from the wet nappy of the child
option_3: Squeeze the nappy of the child into a clean bottle
option_4: Wait for the child to pass urine on the cloth of the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Clean the area of the urinary opening and apply a sterile bag to collect the urine

Clinical Rationale: The area of the urinary opening is cleaned and a sterile bag is applied, because the urine must be free of the germs of the skin and the stool for a culture to be of any use.

Key Clue: urine sample from a 2-year-old child on the ward with a fever who wears a nappy

Priority Principle: Procedure / Urine sample of a child

Why Not Others: (b) Urine from a wet nappy holds the germs of the skin and the stool; (c) Squeezing a nappy mixes the urine with the germs of the stool; (d) Urine passed on a cloth of the bed is not free of the germs of the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because the nappy looks like the ready source of the urine.

5-Second Recall: Chhote bachche ka urine - area saaf karke sterile bag lagao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A culture asks for a urine that has met nothing but a sterile bag.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse manager learns that a staff nurse on the ward has NOT taken the vaccine against an infection of the liver that spreads by blood, though she cares for a client with the infection. Which action should the manager take FIRST?
option_1: Note the matter in the personal file of the nurse and wait
option_2: Move the nurse away from the clients of the ward
option_3: Ask the nurse to wear double gloves for all the care
option_4: Arrange the vaccine for the nurse as per the protocol of the hospital
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Arrange the vaccine for the nurse as per the protocol of the hospital

Clinical Rationale: The manager arranges the vaccine for the nurse as per the protocol, because a staff member who is NOT protected is a danger to herself and to the clients of the ward.

Key Clue: staff nurse on the ward who has NOT taken the vaccine against a liver infection that spreads by blood

Priority Principle: Management / Safety of the staff

Why Not Others: (a) A note in the file leaves the nurse unprotected in the ward; (b) Moving the nurse away does not make her safe against the germ; (c) Double gloves do not guard against every needlestick injury.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a written note looks like the full duty of a manager.

5-Second Recall: Hepatitis B vaccine sabhi staff ke liye - hospital protocol.

PNC Exam Pearl: An unvaccinated staff member is a risk to the whole ward.

question: A nurse teaches a 35-year-old man on the ward who has tuberculosis and sometimes stops his tablets. Which plan is the BEST for the nurse to use to help him finish the course?
option_1: Arrange directly observed therapy with a health worker he trusts for the whole course
option_2: Give him the tablets of the whole month and ask him to be careful
option_3: Tell him the illness will return if he stops and leave it at that
option_4: Ask the family to hide the tablets so that he must ask for each one
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Arrange directly observed therapy with a health worker he trusts for the whole course

Clinical Rationale: Directly observed therapy with a health worker the man trusts keeps the course on track, because a long treatment for tuberculosis is finished only by a man who is supported at every dose.

Key Clue: 35-year-old man on the ward with tuberculosis who sometimes stops his tablets

Priority Principle: Psychosocial / Adherence to treatment

Why Not Others: (b) A month of tablets at home is the way a course is lost; (c) A warning alone does not hold a man through a long course; (d) Hiding the tablets makes the man feel shamed and not helped.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a whole month of tablets looks like the generous help.

5-Second Recall: TB me DOT - bharosemand health worker ke saath roz dawa.

PNC Exam Pearl: A long course is finished with support and not with a warning.

question: A nurse cares for a 4-year-old child on the ward who is on droplet precautions. The child is crying and asks for her mother. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the mother away for the whole stay to stop the spread
option_2: Allow the mother to stay after teaching her the mask and the hand hygiene
option_3: Let the mother come in without a mask, as she is family
option_4: Give the child a sedative so that she stops crying
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Allow the mother to stay after teaching her the mask and the hand hygiene

Clinical Rationale: The mother is taught the mask and the hand hygiene and allowed to stay, because the care of a child on droplet precautions needs her mother and safety is kept by the barrier and NOT by separation.

Key Clue: 4-year-old child on the ward on droplet precautions who is crying and asks for her mother

Priority Principle: Psychosocial / Care of a child on precautions

Why Not Others: (a) A child kept from her mother for the whole stay is left frightened and alone; (c) A mother without a mask takes the droplets of the child herself; (d) A sedative for a child who wants her mother is not the care she needs.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because keeping the family away looks like the strict guard of an infection.

5-Second Recall: Droplet precaution me maa ko mask sikhake andar aane do.

PNC Exam Pearl: A child on precautions still needs her mother.

question: A nurse notes that a newborn of 3 days on the ward has a red and swollen cord stump with a discharge and a poor feed. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Apply an antibiotic powder on the stump and watch it
option_2: Clean the cord with the spirit and record the finding in the chart
option_3: Inform the doctor and prepare the newborn for a test of the blood
option_4: Ask the mother to feed the newborn more often
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Inform the doctor and prepare the newborn for a test of the blood

Clinical Rationale: A red and swollen cord stump with a discharge and a poor feed in a newborn may be an infection that goes into the blood, so the doctor is told and the newborn is prepared for a blood test.

Key Clue: newborn of 3 days on the ward with a red and swollen cord stump, a discharge and a poor feed

Priority Principle: Safety / Infection of the newborn

Why Not Others: (a) A powder on the stump does not touch the infection inside; (b) A clean of the cord does not treat an infection that has spread; (d) More feeds do not help a newborn who may be septic.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because cleaning the cord looks like the whole care of the stump.

5-Second Recall: Naye bachche ki cord laal-sujan + discharge = sepsis ka khatra, doctor bulao.

PNC Exam Pearl: The cord is a door into the blood of a newborn.

question: A nurse teaches a 55-year-old man on the ward who has low immunity how to lower his risk of infection. Which advice is the MOST important?
option_1: Wash the hands often and ask every visitor to wash before coming close
option_2: Avoid all fruits and vegetables for the whole stay
option_3: Wear a mask at every hour of the day and night
option_4: Ask the nurse to clean the room four times a day
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wash the hands often and ask every visitor to wash before coming close

Clinical Rationale: Washing the hands often and asking every visitor to wash before coming close is the MOST important step, because an infection reaches a man with low immunity mostly on the hands of others.

Key Clue: 55-year-old man on the ward with low immunity learning to lower his risk of infection

Priority Principle: Health teaching / Low immunity

Why Not Others: (b) A diet without fruits and vegetables weakens a man who needs them; (c) A mask worn at every hour is not needed and becomes soiled; (d) A clean room cannot guard against the germs that come on the hands.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a mask worn all day looks like the strongest guard.

5-Second Recall: Neutropenia me haath dhona aur visitor se karana - sabse zaroori.

PNC Exam Pearl: An infection reaches a weak man on the hands of others.

question: A nurse finds a spill of blood on the floor of the ward just outside the room of a client on contact precautions. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wipe the spill at once with a dry mop of the ward
option_2: Cover the spill with the disinfectant and let it lie before the clean-up
option_3: Ask the housekeeping staff to clean it without a barrier
option_4: Leave the spill until the end of the shift and warn the clients
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Cover the spill with the disinfectant and let it lie before the clean-up

Clinical Rationale: The spill is covered with the disinfectant and left to act before the clean-up, because the germs of the blood must be killed before the spill is wiped and carried about.

Key Clue: spill of blood on the floor of the ward

Priority Principle: Safety / Spill of blood

Why Not Others: (a) A dry mop spreads the blood and the germs over a wider area; (c) Housekeeping without a barrier takes the germs of the blood home; (d) A spill left for a shift is a risk to every client and every staff member.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because wiping the spill at once looks like the cleanest answer.

5-Second Recall: Blood spill = pehle disinfectant se cover karo, phir saaf karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A spill is disinfected before it is wiped.

question: A nurse reads the report of a 60-year-old man on the ward and sees a germ of the rod family that lives in the gut, grown from his blood. Which step is the MOST appropriate next in the care?
option_1: Give the usual drug of the ward and watch the fever
option_2: Repeat the culture and wait for the next report
option_3: Check the drug to which the germ is sensitive and give it without delay
option_4: Send a stool sample and treat the gut FIRST
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Check the drug to which the germ is sensitive and give it without delay

Clinical Rationale: A germ of the rod family grown from the blood is a dangerous infection of the blood, so the drug to which the germ is sensitive is given without delay rather than the usual drug of the ward.

Key Clue: report of a 60-year-old man on the ward with a rod germ of the gut grown from his blood

Priority Principle: Safety / Infection of the blood

Why Not Others: (a) An unguided drug of the ward may not touch this germ at all; (b) A repeat culture delays a treatment that the report has already guided; (d) The stool is not the source once the germ is in the blood.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because the usual drug of the ward looks like the quick answer.

5-Second Recall: Blood me gut rod = serious sepsis, sensitivity wali dawa turant do.

PNC Exam Pearl: The drug of the blood infection is chosen by the report and not by habit.

question: A nurse on the ward must prepare a blood pressure cuff for use on a client on contact precautions. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Wrap the cuff in a plastic sheet and leave it in the room
option_2: Wipe the cuff once and then use it on the next client without another clean
option_3: Store the cuff with the clean articles of the trolley
option_4: Clean the cuff with the disinfectant of the ward before it is used on the client
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Clean the cuff with the disinfectant of the ward before it is used on the client

Clinical Rationale: The cuff is cleaned with the disinfectant before it is used on a client on contact precautions, because shared equipment carries the germs from one client to the next.

Key Clue: blood pressure cuff prepared for use on a client on contact precautions

Priority Principle: Infection control / Shared equipment

Why Not Others: (a) A cuff wrapped in plastic still holds the germs on its surface; (b) One wipe between two clients leaves the germs of the first on the cuff; (c) An unclean cuff stored with clean articles soils them all.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because a stored cuff looks like a clean cuff.

5-Second Recall: Shared equipment har client ke beech disinfect karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The germs of the ward travel on the equipment as much as on the hands.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse in the immunisation clinic must keep the vaccine of a 2-month-old baby brought by the mother at the right temperature. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the cold chain?
option_1: Keep the vaccine on the table in a bowl of water at room temperature
option_2: Keep the vaccine in the freezer so that it stays colder for longer
option_3: Carry the vaccine in the pocket of the nurse to keep it warm
option_4: Keep the vaccine in the fridge at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and carry it in a cold box with ice packs
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep the vaccine in the fridge at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and carry it in a cold box with ice packs

Clinical Rationale: The vaccine is kept in the fridge at 2 to 8 degrees Celsius and carried in a cold box with ice packs, because a vaccine that freezes or warms loses the power that makes it work.

Key Clue: vaccine for a 2-month-old baby brought by the mother to the immunisation clinic

Priority Principle: Procedure / Cold chain

Why Not Others: (a) A bowl of water at room temperature is far above the safe range; (b) A vaccine left in a freezer loses its power when it freezes; (c) A vaccine carried in a pocket is warmed by the body of the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a colder place looks like a safer place for a vaccine.

5-Second Recall: Vaccine 2-8 degree me rakho, freezer me kabhi nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: A frozen vaccine is a wasted vaccine.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse is teaching the staff of the ward what to do after a needle-stick injury that happened to a nurse caring for a client. Which action should the nurse name FIRST?
option_1: Squeeze the wound hard and apply the spirit on the site
option_2: Cover the wound with a tight bandage before doing anything else
option_3: Let the wound bleed and wash the site with soap and running water at once
option_4: Report the injury at the end of the shift with the other matters
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Let the wound bleed and wash the site with soap and running water at once

Clinical Rationale: The wound is allowed to bleed and the site is washed with soap and running water at once, because the FIRST care of a needle-stick injury is to clean the wound before the care, the report and the tests follow.

Key Clue: teaching the staff what to do after a needle-stick injury

Priority Principle: Safety / Needle-stick injury

Why Not Others: (a) Squeezing the wound hard hurts the tissue and a spirit on the site burns it; (b) A tight bandage over the wound keeps the germs in and the care out; (d) A report at the end of a shift delays the tests that must begin early.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because covering the wound looks like the FIRST care of any injury.

5-Second Recall: Needle-stick = khoon behene do, paani-sabun se dhoyo, turant report karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The first minute decides the care of a needle-stick injury.

question: A community health nurse visits the village where the water of a well has a gut germ, and a mother draws water from it, so the nurse must make it safe for drinking. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Tell the village to use the water after it stands overnight
option_2: Add the calculated amount of bleach to the water and test the chlorine level
option_3: Add a large handful of bleach to the well to be sure of the dose
option_4: Cover the well with a lid and wait for the germ to die by itself
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Add the calculated amount of bleach to the water and test the chlorine level

Clinical Rationale: The calculated amount of bleach is added and the chlorine level is tested, because a dose that is too small leaves the germ alive and a dose that is too large harms the village.

Key Clue: water of a well with a gut germ, to be made safe for drinking

Priority Principle: Community / Chlorination of water

Why Not Others: (a) Water that stands overnight does not lose the germ by itself; (c) A handful of bleach without measure harms the people who drink it; (d) A lid on the well does not kill the germ already in the water.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because more bleach looks like more safety.

5-Second Recall: Well ka paani - naapa hua bleach daalo, chlorine test karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The dose of chlorine is measured and never guessed.

question: A community health nurse visits the village to plan a measles vaccination campaign for every child. Which step should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Find out how many children of the area need the vaccine and where they live
option_2: Order the vaccine for the number of children of the whole block
option_3: Fix the day of the camp before the list of children is ready
option_4: Ask the teachers to send the children to the health centre
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Find out how many children of the area need the vaccine and where they live

Clinical Rationale: The nurse FIRST finds out how many children of the area need the vaccine and where they live, because the plan of a campaign is built on the number and the spread of the children it must reach.

Key Clue: measles vaccination campaign planned by a community health nurse in a village

Priority Principle: Community / Vaccine campaign

Why Not Others: (b) The vaccine for a whole block is ordered after the number is known; (c) A day fixed before the list is ready wastes the effort of the camp; (d) The children who never go to school are missed by a school route.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (c) is chosen because fixing the day looks like the FIRST step of any plan.

5-Second Recall: Campaign se pehle - kitne bachche, kahan rehte hain, pata karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: A campaign is planned on a list and not on a hope.

question: A nurse reads the chart of a 65-year-old woman two days after surgery on the ward and sees a temperature of 38.9 degrees Celsius, a pulse of 110 per minute and a respiratory rate of 24 per minute. What is the MOST likely meaning of these findings?
option_1: The findings are caused by a low room temperature and need no action
option_2: The findings are the expected changes of the second day after surgery
option_3: The findings meet the criteria of a body-wide response to infection and need the doctor at once
option_4: The findings may be the effect of the pain medicine and need a repeat after an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The findings meet the criteria of a body-wide response to infection and need the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: A temperature above 38 degrees Celsius with a fast pulse and a fast breathing meets the criteria of a body-wide response to infection, which needs the doctor at once.

Key Clue: chart of a 65-year-old woman on the ward two days after surgery with a temperature of 38.9 C, a pulse of 110 per minute and a respiratory rate of 24 per minute

Priority Principle: Lab / Body-wide response to infection

Why Not Others: (a) A low room temperature does not raise a temperature and a pulse together; (b) These changes are not the expected changes of the second day after surgery; (d) The pain medicine does not explain the whole picture and cannot wait for an hour.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a fever after surgery looks like the usual course.

5-Second Recall: Temp 38+, pulse 110, RR 24 = sepsis criteria, doctor turant.

PNC Exam Pearl: The body answers an infection with heat, speed and quick breathing together.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 40-year-old man on the ward is to have a bowel operation in an hour and has an order for a drug against the germs before the surgery. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give the drug after the operation when the wound is closed
option_2: Give the drug at the ordered time and note the exact time of the dose
option_3: Hold the drug until the man is fully asleep in the theatre
option_4: Hold the drug unless the man has a fever before the surgery
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give the drug at the ordered time and note the exact time of the dose

Clinical Rationale: The drug against the germs is given at the ordered time before the surgery and the time of the dose is noted, because a drug that is given too early or too late does NOT guard the wound at the moment of the cut.

Key Clue: 40-year-old man on the ward to have a bowel operation in an hour with an order for a drug against the germs before surgery

Priority Principle: Safety / Drug before surgery

Why Not Others: (a) A drug given after the cut misses the moment the wound is open; (c) A drug held until sleep in the theatre is given too late; (d) A fever is not the reason for this drug, which guards the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because a drug after the wound is closed looks like the natural time.

5-Second Recall: Surgery se pehle wali antibiotic - samay pe do, time note karo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The guard against a wound infection is timed to the cut.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward notes that in one week a client and then two more develop an infection of the blood with the same resistant germ. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Inform the infection control team of the ward about the cluster
option_2: Clean the whole ward with the disinfectant at once
option_3: Move the three clients to separate rooms and wait
option_4: Note the cases in the register and continue the usual care
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Inform the infection control team of the ward about the cluster

Clinical Rationale: A cluster of the same resistant germ in one week is reported to the infection control team at once, because a shared source in the ward must be found before more clients are infected.

Key Clue: a client and then two more on the ward in one week with an infection of the blood from the same resistant germ

Priority Principle: Infection control / Cluster of infection

Why Not Others: (b) A clean of the ward is done after the source is found, not before; (c) Moving the clients apart does not find the shared source; (d) A note in the register leaves the source of the cluster untouched.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a clean ward looks like the answer to every infection.

5-Second Recall: Same resistant germ 3 clients me = cluster, infection control team ko batao.

PNC Exam Pearl: A cluster asks where the germ came from and not only where it went.

question: A nurse who wears a ring must give care to a client on the ward. What is the MOST important point for the nurse to understand about the ring?
option_1: A ring may be worn if it is loose and turns on the finger
option_2: A ring has no effect on the germs of the hands if the hands are washed
option_3: A ring of gold kills the germs under it by itself
option_4: A ring shelters the germs under it and stops the hand rub from reaching the skin
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) A ring shelters the germs under it and stops the hand rub from reaching the skin

Clinical Rationale: A ring shelters the germs under it and stops the hand rub from reaching the skin there, so the nurses of a ward give care without rings or other hand jewellery.

Key Clue: nurse who wears a ring and must give care to a client on the ward

Priority Principle: Infection control / Hand jewellery

Why Not Others: (a) A loose ring still shelters the germs and still holds the water; (b) A wash with a ring on leaves the germs that shelter under it; (c) Gold does not kill the germs that collect under a ring.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because a washed hand with a ring looks like a clean hand.

5-Second Recall: Ward me ring, bangle, nail polish - nahi, germs chhupte hain.

PNC Exam Pearl: The germ hides under the ring and under the nail.

question: A nurse on the ward puts on a fitted mask before entering the room of a client on airborne precautions. Which action is the MOST appropriate use of the mask?
option_1: Check the seal of the mask against the face by feeling the air at the edges
option_2: Wear the mask below the nose so that the nurse can breathe easier
option_3: Hang the mask on the neck between two rooms for reuse
option_4: Touch the front of the mask while it is worn and adjust it often
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check the seal of the mask against the face by feeling the air at the edges

Clinical Rationale: The seal of the mask is checked by feeling for air at the edges, because an airborne germ passes through every gap between the mask and the face.

Key Clue: fitted mask worn by a nurse before entering the room of a client on airborne precautions

Priority Principle: Infection control / Fit of the mask

Why Not Others: (b) A mask below the nose leaves the very air the nurse must not breathe; (c) A mask hung on the neck takes the germs of the room to the next client; (d) Touching the front of the mask spoils the mask and the hands together.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because breathing easier looks like the comfort of a long shift.

5-Second Recall: N95 mask - seal check karo, naak dhako, reuse nahi.

PNC Exam Pearl: An airborne germ enters through the smallest gap.

question: A nurse has given an injection to a 30-year-old man on the ward and must dispose of the needle. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Recap the needle carefully with two hands and throw it in the bin
option_2: Drop the needle into the puncture-proof sharps box kept at the point of care
option_3: Bend the needle and put it in the paper bag of the ward
option_4: Keep the needle on the trolley and dispose it at the end of the round
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Drop the needle into the puncture-proof sharps box kept at the point of care

Clinical Rationale: The needle is dropped into the puncture-proof sharps box at the point of care without recapping, because recapping and carrying a used needle cause MOST of the needle-stick injuries of a ward.

Key Clue: needle disposal after an injection given to a 30-year-old man on the ward

Priority Principle: Safety / Sharps disposal

Why Not Others: (a) Recapping a needle with two hands is the commonest cause of a needle-stick injury; (c) A bent needle in a paper bag cuts through and injures the one who carries it; (d) A needle left on a trolley injures the next person who touches it.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (a) is chosen because recapping looks like the careful way to make a needle safe.

5-Second Recall: Needle ko recap na karo, seedha sharps box me daalo.

PNC Exam Pearl: The needle goes into the box and never back into a cap.

question: A nurse on the ward must care for four clients during the round. Which client should the nurse see FIRST?
option_1: A 50-year-old woman waiting for a test of the blood
option_2: A 40-year-old man with a dressing that is due to be changed
option_3: A 70-year-old man two days after a hip operation with a temperature of 38.8 degrees Celsius
option_4: A 35-year-old man who asks for a tablet for pain
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) A 70-year-old man two days after a hip operation with a temperature of 38.8 degrees Celsius

Clinical Rationale: A temperature of 38.8 degrees Celsius in a man two days after a hip operation may be the start of a deep infection of the wound, so the nurse sees him FIRST before the routine dressing, the test and the tablet.

Key Clue: four clients on the ward during the round, one a 70-year-old man two days after a hip operation with a temperature of 38.8 C

Priority Principle: Priority / Infection after surgery

Why Not Others: (a) A client waiting for a test is stable and does not come first; (b) A dressing due at the round is a routine care that can wait; (d) A request for pain medicine is important and is not the first danger.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (d) is chosen because a client in pain looks like the MOST urgent of the four.

5-Second Recall: Priority - surgery ke baad bukhar wale client ko pehle dekho.

PNC Exam Pearl: The infection after surgery speaks before the pain does.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse on the ward must segregate the waste after the care of a client. Which action is the MOST appropriate under the colour code?
option_1: Put the needle in the yellow bag with the soiled dressing
option_2: Put the used gloves and the needle together in the black bin
option_3: Put the used expiry medicine in the blue bag with the gloves
option_4: Put the used gloves in the yellow bag and the needle in the white puncture-proof box
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Put the used gloves in the yellow bag and the needle in the white puncture-proof box

Clinical Rationale: Used gloves are put in the yellow bag for infected plastic waste and the needle in the white puncture-proof box for sharps, which keeps every kind of waste in its own stream.

Key Clue: waste of the ward to be segregated by the nurse

Priority Principle: Safety / Bio-medical waste

Why Not Others: (a) A needle in a soft yellow bag cuts through and injures the cleaner; (b) Gloves and a needle together in a black bin send sharps to the common dump; (c) An expiry medicine belongs to its own stream and not with the gloves.

PGI Exam Trap: Option (b) is chosen because one bin for all the waste looks like the quickest way of a ward.

5-Second Recall: Yellow bag - infected plastic; white box - needle/sharps. Black - general.

PNC Exam Pearl: Every kind of waste goes into its own stream.
